summary: Tenuous atmospheric layers play an important part in applications ranging from modeling atmospheric heat to transportation safety, disaster and hazard response to wildfires and volcanic eruptions. The height and optical properties of atmospheric layers are usually provided by satellite lidar observations. A known challenge in the identification of atmospheric layers is the detection of tenuous clouds and aerosols, which often escape existing layer detection schemes. The problem lies in the discrimination of faint signals from background, especially in situations where stronger reflectors exist within the same regions, during nighttime and daytime conditions. The Density-Dimension Algorithm (DDA) is an auto-adaptive algorithm which has had wide application from the detection of crevasses on ice sheets in ICESat-2 Advanced Topographic Laser Altimeter System (ATLAS) data, to the detection of atmospheric layers in ICESat-2 and CALIPSO lidar data. This paper focuses on the implementation of the DDA for atmospheric lidar data collected by the Cloud-Aerosol Transport System (CATS) aboard the International Space Station (ISS). We aim to demonstrate the versatility of the DDA in detecting a variety of atmospheric layers, with an emphasis on tenuous clouds and aerosols. Layer detection facilitated by the new CATS-DDA is evaluated using airborne data collected with the Cloud Physics Lidar (CPL). Comparisons of CATS-DDA results with detections in the CATS Level 2 Feature Mask product indicate an increased detection capability for tenuous layers and a refined, more realistic representation of atmospheric layers afforded by the high-resolution capabilities of the DDA, which retains the native resolution of the recorded data. Beyond the functionality of the DDA for layer detection in CATS lidar data, results from this paper serve to demonstrate the ability of the DDA to overcome some of the limitations of the CATS instrument. These findings may aid in developing instruments and algorithms for future atmospheric satellite missions, such as NASA FALCON (Fleet for the Atmosphere Linking Commercial Observations with NASA).

title: Retrieval Algorithm for High-Resolution Near-Surface Air Temperature by Fusing Geostationary and Low Earth Orbit Satellite Observations
summary: Near-surface air temperature (NSAT) is needed at both high spatial and high temporal resolution, but no single satellite sensor provides both. This study develops a clear-sky framework that estimates NSAT in near real time on a 30 m grid at 30-min intervals by fusing Geostationary Korea Multi-Purpose Satellite-2A (GK-2A) and Landsat-8 observations. A Taylor expansion-based downscaling algorithm was adapted to update its parameters at every GK-2A scan, and a thermodynamics-based formulation was simplified into an empirical regression of NSAT on land surface temperature (LST), longwave radiation and a moisture proxy derived from the normalized difference moisture index. Its three coefficients are recalibrated every hour against automatic weather station observations. Over southeastern South Korea in 2023, the root-mean-square error (RMSE) was 2.38 °C at stations withheld from calibration and 2.22 °C at the calibration stations, and it increased to 2.82 °C with previous-day coefficients. The downscaling reduced LST errors against Landsat-8 in 14 of 18 scenes but did not measurably change the station-scale NSAT accuracy. The 30 m grid therefore represents surface-type contrasts within each 2 km GK-2A pixel rather than independent thermal information at 30 m, and the product is valid only under clear-sky conditions with real-time AWS data available for hourly recalibration. Each half-hourly field was produced in about 30 s, supporting near-real-time operation.

title: The Past, Present and Possible Future of Thermal Remote Sensing
summary: The number and diversity of thermal infrared observing systems have grown rapidly. This non-exhaustive review compiles an inventory of 185 named thermal infrared instrument designs spanning 390 historical, operational and planned satellite platform deployments. A status audit identified 83 of these deployments as operational on 18 August 2026. Across this orbital record, the finest reported nominal spatial sampling decreased from 55 km for the Medium Resolution Infrared Radiometer aboard TIROS-2 in 1960 to a provider-reported 3.5 m for the mid-wave infrared imager aboard HotSat-2 in 2026. This reduction of more than four orders of magnitude in nominal spatial sampling does not by itself establish improved effective spatial resolution or radiometric performance. Public continuity missions are now complemented by specialized instruments on the International Space Station, commercial small satellites, aircraft, stratospheric balloons, drones and terrestrial systems. This review links these platform histories to the governing physics of emitted radiation, detector and cooling technologies, calibration, atmospheric effects, emissivity and spatial resolution. It also examines the development from classical machine learning to convolutional, recurrent, transformer, diffusion, foundation and vision–language approaches. The selected examples illustrate different levels of adoption across thermal applications rather than a field-wide measure of uptake. These methods support image interpretation, reconstruction and quantitative retrieval, but model-inferred thermal detail, however visually convincing, is not a direct measurement and must be identified and validated as such. As sensor availability expands, scientific comparability increasingly depends on harmonization, cross-sensor transfer, uncertainty characterization and validation in physical units. We recommend three priorities: (i) open, cross-calibrated thermal archives; (ii) models that preserve the distinct physical meanings of thermal variables; and (iii) validation across sensors, regions and seasons using physical units, independent observations and quantified uncertainty.

title: Warming Trends on the Hurd Peninsula of Livingston Island, Antarctica, Between 2000 and 2024, and Improvements in the Estimation of Air Temperature Using C6.1 MODIS LST Data
summary: Analysing the spatial and temporal variability of near-surface air temperature (Ta) is essential for assessing climate change, particularly in polar regions such as the maritime Antarctic, where observational studies remain comparatively scarce. In areas with sparse meteorological networks, satellite observations provide a valuable means of extending station-based analyses and generating spatially distributed Ta maps. This study analyses updated Ta records from six meteorological stations on the Hurd Peninsula, Livingston Island, for 2000–2024, with particular attention to temperature changes since 2016, and evaluates Ta estimation models based on MODIS Terra daytime LST Collection 6.1 data. The analysis of the Ta time series showed significant warming over the complete 2000–2024 period, with trends ranging from 0.53 to 1.27 °C decade−1, and a clear shift towards warming after 2016. While the 2000–2015 period showed spatially contrasting trends, including cooling at JCI, positive trends were observed at all analysed stations during 2016–2024, ranging from 0.40 to 1.33 °C decade−1 and highlighting substantial local variability across the Hurd Peninsula. The global Ta model, developed using data from all six stations and based on MODIS Terra daytime LST and spatiotemporal variables, achieved a performance comparable to that obtained with Collection 6, with R2 = 0.77 and a cross-validated RMSE of 2.23 °C. The results also showed that rigorous filtering of the MODIS LST observations is essential: retaining only good-quality data and excluding observations with |view angle| > 45° substantially reduced dispersion in the Ta–LST relationship and removed unrealistically low LST values. The introduction of this view-angle threshold represents a new filtering step with respect to our previous studies.

title: Pre-, Co-, and Post-Seismic Temporal Deformation of the 2025 Mw5.8 Aheqi Earthquake and Its Blind Thrust Rupture Mechanism: Based on Pre- and Post-Seismic SBAS-InSAR Observations of the Aheqi Earthquake
summary: On 4 December 2025, an MW5.8 earthquake struck Aheqi County, Xinjiang. The epicenter is located approximately 24 km southwest of the 2024 Wushi MW7.0 earthquake, within the hinterland of the Kalpin Tagh fold-and-thrust belt on the western segment of the South Tianshan seismic zone. To clarify the seismogenic characteristics of this earthquake and its dynamic correlation with the strong Wushi MW7.0 earthquake, we constructed a time-series observation dataset covering 22 months before to 5 months after the earthquake based on ascending and descending Sentinel-1A SAR images, and extracted the time-series deformation trend of Aheqi 22 months before the earthquake (after the Wushi earthquake) using the SBAS-InSAR technology. A step term is introduced into the time-series model to eliminate local unwrapping errors and residual atmospheric delays caused by severe convective weather in the summer of June 2025, so as to obtain a reliable net LOS trend during the observation period. Combined with the co-seismic line-of-sight deformation field acquired by the two-pass D-InSAR method, a comprehensive study is carried out by integrating distributed fault slip inversion and Coulomb stress change simulation. The results show the following: (1) The co-seismic deformation is dominated by positive LOS displacement (motion toward the satellite), with maximum LOS deformations of approximately 5.0 cm and 6.0 cm for the ascending and descending orbits, respectively. The deformation field presents a significantly asymmetric elliptical shape with no surface rupture, indicating a blind thrust rupture. (2) SBAS time-series analysis for the 22 months preceding the earthquake reveals tectonic rates of approximately +26.9 mm/yr for the hanging wall and +8.5 mm/yr for the footwall, yielding a net across-fault LOS velocity difference over the observation window of ∼18.4 mm/yr. We note that the first SAR acquisition in our pre-seismic time series (February 2024) occurs only ∼12 days after the 2024 Wushi Mw7.0 earthquake (22 January 2024). Consequently, the estimated linear trend inherently captures a superposition of possible early post-seismic transient deformation and interseismic tectonic loading. We therefore interpret the ∼18.4 mm/yr difference as the net across-fault LOS velocity difference over the observation window. This value is compatible with, but does not independently verify, long-term elastic strain accumulation on the Aheqi fault. (3) The inverted seismogenic fault has a strike of approximately 242°, a dip angle of approximately 40°, a slip angle of approximately 74°, a centroid depth of approximately 6.2 km, a maximum slip of approximately 0.17 m, and a moment magnitude of MW5.9. The rupture is dominated by thrust motion with a minor strike-slip component, the exact direction of which is not fully constrained, indicating that the Aheqi fault is the likely seismogenic structure of this earthquake. (4) The Coulomb stress calculation results show that the 2024 Wushi MW7.0 earthquake produced a static stress loading of more than 2 bar in the source region of the Aheqi fault, far exceeding the earthquake empirical reference threshold of 0.1 bar. Combining the pre-seismic strain accumulation characteristics, co-seismic slip distribution and Coulomb stress calculation results, we suggest that the Aheqi earthquake—a moderate blind thrust event—may have been promoted by static stress loading from the 2024 Wushi MW7.0 earthquake, superimposed on long-term tectonic loading. While the exact time-dependent triggering process (including the 22-month delay) requires further viscoelastic or pore-pressure diffusion modeling, the static Coulomb stress analysis confirms a positive loading of >2 bar. The results of this study can provide measured deformation constraints and reference for analyzing the seismogenic mechanism of the structural transition zone in the piedmont of South Tianshan and improving the regional seismotectonic model.

title: Physics-Driven Deep Learning for ISAR Imaging of Maneuvering Targets with a Large Rotation Angle
summary: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) is important for space target surveillance and recognition. However, under large rotation angles and uniformly accelerated target rotation, coupled high-order migration through range cells (MTRC) and two-dimensional space-variant phase errors cannot be accurately compensated by conventional methods based on small-angle or constant-rotation assumptions, causing image defocusing. To address this, a physics-driven subaperture differentiable back-projection (BP) ISAR imaging network is proposed. It embeds a parametric rotation model with angular velocity and acceleration: taking complex-valued HRRP sequences as input, the full aperture is partitioned into overlapping subapertures, and rotation parameters are regressed by a cross-subaperture parameter estimation network exploiting local scattering structures, temporal correlations, and motion evolution features; a differentiable BP imaging layer unifies rotation transformation, slant-range computation, complex-valued interpolation, phase compensation, and coherent accumulation into differentiable tensor operations, allowing image-domain losses to backpropagate to the parameter estimation module for closed-loop joint optimization of parameter estimation and focusing quality; and a phase registration and quality-guided coherent fusion mechanism adaptively suppresses sidelobes, defocusing, and noise from low-quality subapertures. Experiments on point-scatterer and electromagnetic simulation models demonstrate clear advantages, particularly at low SNR, providing a new path for high-resolution ISAR imaging of large-angle maneuvering targets.

title: Experimental Study of Spectral Radiometric Correction for Underwater 3D-Imaging by Hyperspectral LiDAR
summary: Hyperspectral LiDAR (HSL) has emerged as a cutting-edge technique for underwater 3D imaging. Nevertheless, wavelength-selective absorption and scattering of light by water induce severe distortion in the spectral information of submerged targets and further result in color casts. In this paper, the underwater target spectral radiometric correction (UWSRC) method is adopted to correct the spectral reflectance of underwater targets by combining pre-measured water spectral transmittance and range data acquired by LiDAR. This approach obviates the complicated in situ measurement of water inherent optical parameters, which reduces the operational complexity for field deployments of underwater hyperspectral LiDAR remote sensing. Its spectral correction capability is experimentally validated under varying detection distances and diverse aquatic environments, including clear tap water and eutrophic turbid water. Furthermore, a dedicated HSL prototype for underwater scanning and a semi-submerged pod are developed. With this prototype, the 3D scanning imaging distance can be extended to 5.3 m in an outdoor swimming pool. Experimental results demonstrate that the UWSRC method can effectively compensate for the spectral reflectance of underwater targets under different water qualities and detection ranges. Meanwhile, true-color 3D point clouds of a color-calibration board are successfully obtained during long-distance scanning. Error analysis of reflectance inversion is carried out to explore the sensitivity to water transmittance bias and ranging uncertainty. The experimental investigations in this paper verify that the UWSRC method achieves favorable performance in underwater target spectral restoration and true-color reconstruction across different water qualities and detection distances.

title: Class-Conditioned Evidence Recovery in Frozen Vision Transformers for Remote Sensing Object Detection
summary: Aerial object detectors must resolve small, closely spaced objects while retaining enough context to recognize large structures. RS-Adapter uses an image-level class prior to update intermediate features in a frozen vision transformer. The prior combines a learned classifier, fixed class prototypes, and class-conditional descriptor statistics. Cross-attention links the prior to local features, which are fused across scales and gated before being added to the transformer. The adapted features guide a denoiser that generates box prompts for the detection decoder. On VisDrone, RS-Adapter achieved 39.2% average precision (AP) and 28.4% small-object AP, 3.1 percentage points above DEIM-D-FINE-L on the latter metric. AP50 was 78.3% on DIOR, 84.5% on NWPU VHR-10, and 87.7% on RSOD. RS-Adapter trained 16.8 million of its 103.2 million parameters and used less peak training memory than full tuning in the VisDrone comparison.

title: Recovery-Error-Bound-Guided Frequency Selection for Moving-Target Microwave Coincidence Imaging
summary: In microwave coincidence imaging (MCI), radiation patterns with low mutual correlation, generated by an appropriately selected frequency set, provide spatial diversity for high-resolution imaging. For moving targets, however, residual state-prediction errors after motion compensation can still cause a mismatch between the echoes and the observation matrix, degrading imaging performance despite this spatial diversity. To improve imaging robustness under this mismatch, frequency-set selection is guided by a conditional upper bound on the scattering-coefficient recovery error. This bound accounts for both the sensitivity of the observation matrix to state-prediction errors and the distinguishability of sparse scatterers. The state-prediction-error tolerance is chosen such that this bound does not exceed a prescribed recovery-error threshold. The frequency set is then selected by maximizing the minimum tolerance over the prescribed observation conditions. The resulting frequency set is used for closed-loop tracking and imaging with a frequency-diverse metasurface. During closed-loop operation, the predicted state is used to form the observation matrix, and the image centroid is fed back to update the state estimate. This update incorporates the correlation between state-prediction errors and image-derived observation errors. Simulation results show that, at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 10dB and an x-direction offset of 0.08m, the success rate for resolving two targets separated by 1.83∘ increases from 20% with uniform frequency sampling to 80% with the selected frequency set. For an extended target at 0dB SNR, the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), evaluated against a stationary-target reference reconstruction, improves by 1.5dB, and the scatterer-localization root-mean-square error (RMSE) for matched detections decreases by 71.8% compared with uniform frequency sampling. These results demonstrate that the proposed criterion improves resolution, image quality, and localization accuracy in the presence of state-prediction errors, without increasing the number of operating frequencies.

title: A Novel Deep Learning Network for Fractional Vegetation Cover Calculation Using Full-Waveform LiDAR
summary: Traditional fractional vegetation cover (FVC) calculation methods relying solely on either airborne LiDAR waveforms or point clouds often suffer from degraded performance due to single-modality limitations and spatially uneven point density. To address this issue, this study proposes a multimodal fusion network termed the joint LiDAR waveform and point-cloud network (JWP-Net) and a 2D grid area ratio-based FVC calculation method. First, with a high-resolution digital orthophoto map as an auxiliary reference, an interactive human–machine visual interpretation workflow is adopted to precisely label LiDAR echoes into three categories: vegetation, land, and water. A standardized dataset is thereby established for subsequent data analysis and model training. Second, a novel deep learning network termed JWP-Net, which utilizes LiDAR echo waveforms and point clouds as multimodal inputs, is proposed to classify the laser points into vegetation, land, and water. Third, a 2D grid area ratio-based FVC calculation method is proposed to calculate the FVC based on the classified laser points. To validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework, experiments are conducted using raw measurement data acquired by the Optech Aquarius LiDAR system. Experimental results demonstrate that JWP-Net achieves an overall classification accuracy of 94.00% ± 0.41% (mean value ± standard deviation of 5-fold overall accuracies evaluated on the untouched held-out test grids), outperforming single-modal models by 1.77–2.52%. Furthermore, integrating DBSCAN-based spatial morphological smoothing on the held-out grids steadily improves the overall classification accuracy to 94.81% ± 0.44%. Moreover, compared with the traditional laser point-count-based FVC calculation method, the proposed 2D grid area ratio-based method reduces the FVC absolute deviation by 3 percentage points on test grids at a 0.2 m grid resolution. The multimodal fusion strategy that combines airborne laser full-waveform and point-cloud data, and the 2D grid area-ratio-based FVC calculation method proposed in this work, offer a novel research approach for high-precision FVC calculation using full-waveform LiDAR.

title: Groundwater Depletion Linked to Vegetation Restoration in the Mongolian Plateau
summary: Groundwater constitutes a vital component of the water resources of the Mongolian Plateau (MP), supplying water for industrial, agricultural, domestic, and ecological uses while sustaining the local ecosystems. However, the long-term patterns of groundwater storage change and their environmental associations remain incompletely understood. In this study, we quantified groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA) from 2003 to 2023 using data from the GRACE/GRACE-FO gravity satellites and the Global Land Data Assimilation System (GLDAS), which revealed a marked regional decline of 0.322 cm yr−1. By employing a random forest model that accounts for both climate-related and human-induced factors, we identified precipitation (Pre), surface runoff (SurR), potential evapotranspiration (PET), and vegetation greening (increases in NDVI) as the key drivers of groundwater depletion. Further analysis through multiple linear regression revealed the spatially varying impacts of Pre, SurR, and PET, with groundwater changes in western Mongolia and southern Inner Mongolia exhibiting strong spatial correlations with PET. In southern Inner Mongolia—a desert region and a focal area of China-led large-scale ecological restoration—this association likely reflects the increased PET and the ecological water use sourced from groundwater, both induced by vegetation restoration efforts. These findings indicate that large-scale vegetation restoration in water-limited regions could significantly strain groundwater resources. Therefore, integrating groundwater management into ecological restoration strategies is essential for sustaining the long-term resilience of both ecosystems and regional environments.

title: G3H-GraphSim: A Reproducible 3D GeoHash Cell-Graph Workflow for Semantic LiDAR Analysis
summary: Reliable infrastructure graph analysis requires transparent links between point-cloud observations, semantic annotations, spatial addresses, and graph decisions. This study evaluates G3H-GraphSim, a reproducible three-dimensional GeoHash cell-graph workflow on five adjacent Gwangju LAS–annotation tiles, using shared-origin metric grids, stage-level computational measurements, and tile-resolved paired routing statistics. Tile-local level-7 cells have unequal physical dimensions and largest-component shares of 26.0–95.1%. In a pooled grid with 4 m × 4 m horizontal cells, six-neighbor largest-component shares are 24.7% at 0.5 m and 26.5% at 1.0 m vertical resolution, showing that common addressing alone does not ensure graph continuity. A noncontemporaneous OpenStreetMap cross-check places 95.3% of retained road-cell centers within 10 m of mapped centerlines, although only 63.5% of selected reference-line length is covered. On the same 150 start–goal pairs, integrated routing reduces pooled mean speed-bump proximity and high-LiDAR-density cell entries by 18.0% and 28.5%, respectively, at a 0.6% increase in mean route length, with appreciable tile-to-tile variation. Stage-level tests show lower amortized batch exact-key lookup time and smaller key-array payload for packed integers than for padded Base32 strings. The results demonstrate traceable sensitivity to spatial resolution, representation, and routing policy, without establishing field-calibrated safety or deployed-system performance.

title: IntentCD: Remote Sensing Change Detection Guided by Implicit User Intent
summary: Remote sensing change detection (CD) is commonly formulated as pixel-level localization of predefined changes or changes specified by explicit semantic categories. However, practical users often express their requirements indirectly through functional, causal, or consequence-oriented descriptions, creating a semantic gap between natural-language intent and the corresponding spatiotemporal change regions. Our introduces implicit user-intent-guided change detection and proposes IntentCD, an intent-aware multimodal framework that translates indirect user requirements into pixel-level change maps. The key idea is to use a latent change-of-interest representation to bridge intent interpretation and temporal change localization. Specifically, bi-temporal remote sensing images and user instructions are jointly encoded into a multimodal representation, while a pretrained large language model is employed to infer implicit user intent from implicit descriptions. The inferred semantic representation is then used to condition a change-map decoder, which integrates high-level semantic features and multi-scale visual features for pixel-level change localization. Experiments are conducted on the BCDD and SECOND datasets. On BCDD, IntentCD achieves an F1 score of 92.1% for building change detection. In addition, implicit-intent annotations derived from multiple land-cover categories in SECOND are used to evaluate the model under indirect semantic descriptions. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can generate change maps conditioned on both explicit and implicit user requirements while maintaining competitive change detection performance. These findings suggest that incorporating implicit user intent provides a more flexible interface between natural-language requirements and remote sensing change analysis.

title: Cross-Sensor NDVI Consistency and Multi-Scale Vegetation Dynamics in the Northern Qinling Piedmont (China)
summary: Vegetation dynamics in heterogeneous mountain–plain transition zones may be represented differently by satellite sensors with contrasting spatial and temporal characteristics. This study evaluated NDVI derived from Landsat, MODIS, and Sentinel-2 in the Northern Qinling Piedmont, China, and investigated vegetation changes across complementary spatiotemporal scales. The three datasets showed substantial spatial and seasonal consistency, while differences in NDVI magnitude, short-term temporal variations, and data completeness were also observed. Although the original monthly time series exhibited high inter-sensor correlations, these correlations decreased substantially after removing seasonal effects, indicating that shared seasonal variations accounted for much of the apparent temporal agreement. Sentinel-2 and MODIS exhibited higher data availability than Landsat during 2021–2025. Considering its continuous long-term record and relatively high data availability, MODIS was used to characterize long-term vegetation changes during 2001–2025, while Sentinel-2 was used to resolve recent fine-scale changes during 2019–2025. Regional NDVI increased significantly, with pronounced greening mainly in the eastern and southern areas. For the long-term record, declining or non-significant trends were concentrated mainly in urbanized areas, whereas recent Sentinel-2 observations revealed localized NDVI declines in the western Qinling piedmont floodplain. NDVI was positively associated with temperature and precipitation, with stronger relationships in spring. Precipitation showed its strongest positive association with NDVI over a three-month accumulation window. Topographic conditions and land-use/land-cover changes were also associated with spatial and temporal heterogeneity in vegetation dynamics. These results show that broad regional greening can coexist with localized vegetation decline and highlight the importance of matching satellite sensor characteristics with monitoring scales in heterogeneous ecological transition zones.

title: Sparse Height Sampling of Radar Wind-Profile Products: Criterion-Dependent Sufficiency and Temporal Stability
summary: Wind-profile products are often reported on dense vertical grids, while neighbouring levels can share substantial covariance. This study quantifies the number and placement of reported heights needed to reconstruct a 15-level, 10 min mean horizontal wind-speed (WS_MEAN) radar product spanning 20–300 m under explicit root-mean-square error (RMSE) criteria. Historical profiles were used for proper orthogonal decomposition with QR-based height selection (POD–QR), and performance was evaluated in six forward-chaining windows against endpoint-matched layouts and a training-only exhaustive subset analysis. The all-six-fold POD–QR minimum was 14, 10, 5, and 3 retained levels at RMSE tolerances of 0.30, 0.40, 0.50 and 0.70 m s−1, respectively. At 0.50 m s−1, five levels achieved a mean RMSE of 0.395 m s−1 and ranked within the best 5.94% of endpoint-matched layouts in every fold. Seven levels reduced mean RMSE to 0.328 m s−1, with 91.3% of profiles below 0.50 m s−1. Early-fold layouts retained comparable performance in later periods, while profile curvature, level availability, and observation noise systematically affected recoverability. These findings support accuracy-constrained wind-profile product design and height-channel prioritisation, with potential applications in reduced-height sampling, missing-level reconstruction, data quality checks, and reduced transmission and storage requirements.

title: Task-Oriented Evaluation of PolSAR Despeckling for Downstream Applications
summary: Polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) records multiple polarization channels to characterize target scattering, but its coherent imaging mechanism produces multiplicative speckle that complicates downstream analysis. Existing despeckling methods pursue different objectives, so visual inspection and conventional image-quality metrics may not reflect their practical utility. In this work, six representative conventional and deep-learning-based despeckling methods and the unfiltered data are evaluated through three downstream tasks: land-cover classification on three scenes, ice-type classification on a GaoFen-3 scene, and CFAR-based ship detection on offshore images of the FPSD dataset. Each task depends on a different property of the filtered covariance data, so the same despeckled product can suit one task and not another: NL-SAR gives the highest land-cover accuracy on two scenes but ranks sixth of seven inputs in ship detection, whereas SDNLM attains the highest calibrated detection F1 but ranks sixth of seven on the Island scene. This task dependence persists under targeted sensitivity analyses of smoothing strength, classifier choice, covariance validity, and detector calibration. Despeckling methods should therefore be evaluated against the information that the intended downstream task requires and selected on that basis, rather than by visual quality or a single task-independent criterion.

title: UAV Multispectral Monitoring of Foliar Biostimulant Strips in Sunflower Under On-Farm Conditions in a Drought Year, Supported by Sentinel-2 Time Series
summary: Foliar biostimulants are widely used in sunflower to mitigate abiotic stress, but their on-farm evaluation is hampered by unreplicated strip designs and field variability. In an exploratory, unreplicated on-farm strip trial, we compared four commercial biostimulants (Amalgerol, Auronik, Natural Force and Dell Agro plus) in an 8 ha sunflower field in central Hungary during the exceptionally dry 2026 season (April–September precipitation 40% of the long-term mean). Multispectral UAV images were acquired on the day of treatment, at flowering and at the yellow-back-of-head stage, and NDVI, NDRE, GNDVI and LCI were analysed for 12 digital sampling boxes per strip with baseline-referenced statistics, repeated-measures ANOVA and Cohen’s d. At treatment, no differences between the strips were detected (p ≥ 0.39). Thereafter, they diverged in the order Dell Agro plus > Natural Force > Auronik > Amalgerol: the change in GNDVI to flowering differed among strips (p = 0.002; Holm-adjusted p = 0.013), and at the final stage Dell Agro plus exceeded Amalgerol by 15.5% in NDVI (d = 1.07–1.31 across indices), retained the most greenness and showed the smallest increase in canopy heterogeneity. A Sentinel-2 time series agreed with the UAV data at all three dates (r = 0.71–0.92) and showed the same post-treatment ranking. Single-date comparisons did not reveal these differences. Because the strips were neither randomised nor replicated and no untreated control was included, the differences cannot be attributed unequivocally to the products; a pre-treatment flight and baseline-referenced analysis are nevertheless essential for describing on-farm biostimulant strip trials.

title: Coupled Mechanisms Between Permafrost Degradation and Vegetation Dynamics in a Typical Alpine Catchment of the Qilian Mountains over the Past Four Decades
summary: Under a warming climate, the impact of alpine permafrost degradation on vegetation dynamics is crucial for understanding ecosystem evolution. Drawing on long-term multi-source observational data from 1986 to 2025 and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), this study investigated the coupled mechanisms between permafrost degradation and vegetation dynamics in a typical alpine catchment of the Qilian Mountains. The results demonstrated that: (1) Over the past four decades, permafrost in the study area exhibited a continuous degradation pattern, with its areal extent decreasing from 92.5% to 73.8% at a rate of approximately 0.53% yr−1. This degradation was characterized by spatial heterogeneity, showing preferential degradation in the southern region and intensified fragmentation in the central region. (2) The study area experienced an overall significant greening trend. Between 2021 and 2025, areas with high vegetation coverage (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) ≥ 0.09) accounted for 66.4% of the total area, and the greening rate was significantly but only partly modulated by local topography. (3) The permafrost thermal regime exerted a pronounced gradient effect on vegetation dynamics. Vegetation improvement was most rapid in Degraded Permafrost zones, and the promoting effect of active layer deepening on vegetation growth exhibited an optimal threshold of approximately 1.2 m. (4) The freeze-state index showed the strongest statistical association with vegetation dynamics (β = −0.56), whereas the direct precipitation effect was negligible (β = −0.01); the two climate variables co-vary along the elevational gradient and cannot be separated here. Current greening has benefited from hydrothermal conditions released during early permafrost degradation, but this effect may weaken as ground ice is depleted.

title: Dark Vessel Detection Agent: Evidence-Driven Screening and Verification Task Generation Using Satellite Imagery and AIS
summary: Dark vessels that deactivate their Automatic Identification System (AIS) or conceal their identities pose substantial challenges to maritime monitoring. A central scientific problem is whether satellite–AIS mismatch can be interpreted as direct evidence of non-cooperative vessel activity, or whether its evidential meaning must be resolved through spatiotemporal AIS support and maritime geographic context. To address this problem, we develop an evidence-driven Dark Vessel Detection Agent that formulates suspected dark-vessel screening as a target-level evidence-interpretation process. The framework integrates Gaofen-6 vessel-like target detection using YOLOv11 oriented bounding boxes, historical AIS-derived navigation context, rule-based geospatial reasoning, DeepSeek-V4-assisted evidence-consistency review, and image-time AIS trajectory rechecking. In the Pearl River Estuary, China, 825 AIS-unexplained targets were reduced to 361 reviewed candidates. Image-time trajectory assessment subsequently identified 114 candidates as AIS-spatiotemporally explainable, while 247 remained unresolved and were retained as prioritized verification tasks, reducing the initial candidate pool by 70.06%. Selective AIS querying reduced query volume by 32.41% relative to exhaustive rechecking and identified 65.14% of the cases meeting the closure criterion. These results show that satellite–AIS mismatch is not a self-sufficient indicator of non-cooperative vessel activity. Its evidential meaning emerges from the joint interpretation of remote-sensing observations, image-time AIS trajectory support, and maritime geographic context.

title: Parameter-Efficient Multilingual Vision–Language Adaptation for Spatio-Temporal Climate-Risk Interpretation from Satellite Imagery
summary: Climate-risk monitoring requires models that connect satellite observations with natural-language questions while supporting users working in different languages. We present ClimateRS-VL, a parameter-efficient adaptation of Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct for English, Gujarati, and Hindi climate-risk interpretation. The benchmark combines 7182 regional optical–mask pairs from six districts of Gujarat, 1026 nominal regional temporal pairs, 740 reservoir-year metadata records, 409 reservoir-year image samples, and 178,503 programmatically generated multilingual references. A prompt audit confirms that explicit answer-bearing numerical and categorical variables were absent from all 126,810 training, 25,854 validation, and 25,839 test prompts. On the full 25,839-response test evaluation, English, Gujarati, and Hindi VQA obtain BLEU scores of 83.9230, 80.9125, and 83.2524, with BERTScore-F1 values of 0.9891, 0.9961, and 0.9953. A same-backbone study on a common 3000-response subset yields an average VQA BLEU of 0.5625 for zero-shot Qwen2.5-VL, 1.1138 with contextual prompting but no adaptation, and 85.5191 with contextual prompting and LoRA. Question-aligned cross-lingual consistency is 0.9673, although this metric measures agreement rather than correctness. Class-balanced analysis further shows that raw accuracies above 0.98 on four regional risk questions arise from severe low-risk class prevalence: the model predicts the low-risk class for every sample, yielding a balanced accuracy of 0.5000. The protocol is a temporal holdout over recurring monitoring locations rather than an evaluation of unseen-location generalization. The results support parameter-efficient multilingual adaptation for structured in-domain generation while identifying limitations in numerical visual reasoning, minority-risk discrimination, reference diversity, and spatial generalization.

title: State SoilMERGE: Downscaling Root Zone Soil Moisture with Tree-Based and Deep Learning Models
summary: Soil moisture regulates water and energy exchange between the land surface and the atmosphere, yet most current satellite products have a resolution on the order of tens of kilometers. SoilMERGE (SMERGE) is a 0.125° root zone soil moisture product covering the contiguous United States based on fusion of satellite and land model datasets. Building on earlier tree-based downscaling work, 500 m versions of SMERGE across Kansas, Oklahoma, North Texas, and South Texas were produced. Three comparisons were evaluated: per-state vs. pooled models, land cover as an input variable, and deep learning vs. tree-based models with five algorithms: Yggdrasil Decision Forests random forest (YDFRF) and XGBoost (XGB) as tree-based models. Deep learning models included Gated Linear Units (GLU), TabNet, and a tabular network derived from the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT). All downscaled products showed improved ranked correlation with AVHRR/VIIRS NDVI compared to the original SMERGE, with the best per-region model raising the ranked correlation coefficient by 0.04 to 0.09 while preserving fidelity to the default SMERGE (anomaly RMSE 0.0136 to 0.0231 m3/m3). In Kansas and Oklahoma, per-state and pooled models performed similarly (mean matched-pixel ΔR −0.016 to +0.007; equivalent within ±0.02 for every model under a spatial block bootstrap). Adding land cover as an input changed the ranked correlation by 0.0053 on average in absolute value. Evaluated through agreement with vegetation response, these results support further development of a state-based 500 m version of SMERGE in the Southern Great Plains.

title: A Meta-Analysis of Reported Performance of Reflectance- and Solar-Induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence-Based Approaches for Estimating Vegetation Gross Primary Productivity
summary: Accurate estimation of gross primary productivity (GPP) is essential for monitoring terrestrial photosynthesis and ecosystem responses to environmental change. We synthesized 81 studies retrieved from the Web of Science to explore reported performance patterns of spectral reflectance- and solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF)-based GPP estimation. Approaches were classified by the GPP predictors and their provenance, distinguishing reflectance-based estimates from those based on observation-retrieved SIF. Mean study-level R2 values were 0.691 for reflectance-based approaches and 0.661 for SIF-based approaches, with no significant difference between them (p = 0.384). Both approaches exhibited substantial between-study heterogeneity and distinct temporal responses. Subgroup analyses examined vegetation type, environmental stress, and temporal resolution. SIF-based pooled R2 was lower under stress than under non-stress conditions (0.525 versus 0.735; p = 0.020). Reflectance-based pooled R2 also decreased numerically, from 0.719 to 0.625, but the difference was not significant (p = 0.499). Reflectance-based pooled R2 was highest for C4 crops, whereas differences among vegetation types were not significant for SIF-based approaches. Weekly SIF-based estimates had a higher pooled R2 than subdaily estimates (0.736 versus 0.652; p = 0.023). Incorporating canopy structure and soil water content was associated with the largest reported mean relative improvements in R2 for reflectance- and SIF-based approaches, respectively. These findings support selecting GPP estimation approaches according to vegetation type, environmental conditions, and temporal scale, and combining reflectance and SIF with relevant structural and environmental information.

title: Spatial Transition in Surface Particulate Organic Carbon Seasonality in the Changjiang Estuary and Adjacent Waters
summary: Rivers deliver particulate organic carbon (POC) to the coastal ocean together with suspended sediment, yet it remains unclear whether the seasonal cycle of surface POC follows that of the suspended-particle field. We combined monthly Sentinel-3 Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI) POC for 2022–2025, hourly Geostationary Ocean Color Imager-II (GOCI-II) observations, and field data in the Changjiang Estuary and the adjacent East China Sea. The OLCI POC retrieval yielded a root-mean-square error of 0.288 dex in log10 POC against 96 station-scene matchups, and a residual-fusion algorithm transferred the OLCI concentration level to hourly GOCI-II observations. Retrieved POC peaked in summer near the estuary and in winter farther seaward. These two annual cycles were nearly opposite, and their equal-weight midpoint lay approximately 46 km seaward of the maximum logarithmic gradient of total suspended solids (TSS) (95% year-resampling interval, 40–53 km). Between the two regimes, the annual amplitude reached its minimum, and morning–afternoon differences in the fused fields were comparable to the annual amplitude. Near the estuary, field POC was higher in summer, when TSS was lower, identifying the summer maximum as a carbon signal. Over the outer shelf, field POC showed no cold-season increase despite higher TSS, indicating that the winter maximum includes an optical effect of particle composition. Field POC increased sublinearly with TSS, such that the carbon content of suspended particles decreased with increasing TSS.

title: Spatiotemporal Patterns and Drivers of Multiple Forest Change Types in China’s Tropical and Subtropical Regions
summary: Tropical and subtropical forests harbor over half of the world’s terrestrial biodiversity and account for a large fraction of the global terrestrial carbon sink. However, under accelerating climate change and human pressure, the dynamics of these forests remain incompletely characterized, particularly in rapidly developing regions where multiple change processes—fire, clear-cutting, afforestation, and deforestation—operate simultaneously. Using 30 m Landsat time-series imagery spanning 1993–2021, fused with China’s annual land-cover dataset (CLCD) and the continuous change-detection algorithm (CCDC), this study constructed a unified, multi-type forest-change dataset for tropical and subtropical China. The spatiotemporal patterns of four dominant change types were quantified through grid-based intensity analysis and the Mann–Kendall trend test, and associations with annual intensity classes were examined using an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) ensemble learner combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) model interpretation. Our results reveal the following: First, spatially, fire and clear-cutting both exhibit a southeast–southwest dual-core aggregation pattern, while afforestation and deforestation show highly congruent, largely dispersed distributions dominated by the moderate period-summary intensity class. Second, temporally, fire shows an overall declining trend, with 52.1% of grid cells exhibiting significant or non-significant decreases; clear-cutting shows significant increases in 28.4% of grid cells. Afforestation and deforestation are both dominated by significant and non-significant increases: 48.7% and 62.8% of grid cells, respectively. For deforestation, 44.8% of the grids included in the peak-year analysis reached their maximum annual intensity during 2011–2015, although this concentration may partly reflect temporal inconsistencies in the underlying CLCD data. Third, the annual intensity-class models identify potential evapotranspiration as a leading predictor for fire and mean temperature as an important environmental covariate for clear-cutting. Slope and population are important predictors for both afforestation and deforestation. In the spatial summaries of SHAP contributions to the annual high-intensity class output, slope is a prominent negative contributor, particularly for afforestation and deforestation. This study provides a unified, multi-type, multi-decade analysis of forest change in tropical and subtropical China, characterizes nonlinear associations with annual intensity-class outputs, and maps their dominant positive and negative SHAP contributors to support precision forest management and climate-adaptive ecological policy design.

title: RDF-Det: Robust Dual-Path Fusion for CNN-Based Vehicle Fire Detection in Ground-Based RGB Imagery
summary: Road incidents involving public-transport vehicles and hazardous-material carriers require ground-based RGB sensing capable of localizing full vehicle extent while identifying visible fire cues under severe background clutter, scale variation, and illumination artifacts. To address the tension between preserving macro-level vehicle semantics and capturing localized fire patterns, we propose the Robust Dual-Path Fusion Detector (RDF-Det), centered on a parallel feature-fusion neck (RDF-Neck) that integrates top–down semantic propagation with bidirectional spatial aggregation. By decoupling the dual-path topology from branch-mixing parameterization, we systematically investigate four routing strategies—level-wise learned, globally shared, fixed-uniform, and parameter-matched frozen routing—and evaluate cross-family instantiations across RTMDet, YOLOX, and Faster R-CNN. Across a 100-run five-seed benchmark, the main RDF-Det configuration (RTM-RDF-GLR-DINO) achieves mean validation scores of 0.6352 AP and 0.9290 AP50, delivering a system-level improvement of 7.24 AP points over RTM-Base and outperforming the YOLO26 detector (0.6235 AP and 0.9071 AP50). Controlled evaluations on both the validation split and a screened test subset demonstrate that lightweight global and fixed-uniform fusion remain highly competitive with complex level-wise routing, while cross-family comparisons clarify the architectural conditions governing one-stage and two-stage adaptation. Supported by repeated runs, confidence intervals, and Holm-corrected paired tests, this study provides both an effective vehicle-fire detection framework and systematic empirical insights into dual-path multi-scale fusion.

title: Spatiotemporal Dual-Polarization Radar Quantitative Precipitation Estimation Using Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: Hourly quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) from weather radar remains difficult during intense rainfall because fixed empirical relations and temporal averaging may not represent rapid scan-to-scan changes and localized echo structure. We evaluated five convolutional neural network configurations using S-band dual-polarization radar and rain-gauge observations in Guangzhou, China. A locally calibrated composite dual-polarization estimator (Composite-DP) provided a conventional reference. Each sample contains ZH, ZDR, and KDP from ten consecutive 0.5° scans over the preceding hour in a 3 × 10 × 21 × 21 tensor. Three-dimensional convolution spans time and two horizontal dimensions, without vertical-volume input. The dataset from 2018 to 2021 comprised 3,008,738 matched samples with rainfall ≥ 0.1 mm h−1, including 2,611,457 for training, 149,221 from six 2020 events for validation, and 141,428 from six 2021 events for testing. The models included a temporally averaged 2D baseline (2DPoly-QPENet), a time-resolved 3D baseline (3DPoly-QPENet), separate temporal (3DTime-QPENet) and multiscale (3DEcho-QPENet) extensions, and their fusion (3DHybrid-QPENet). The temporal extension represented the encoded ten-step sequence with a convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) layer, whereas the multiscale extension used an encoder–decoder pathway. On the independent test set, Composite-DP yielded an RMSE of 4.139 mm h−1. Compared with 2DPoly-QPENet, 3DPoly-QPENet had a lower mean absolute error (MAE; 1.321 versus 1.524 mm h−1) and root-mean-square error (RMSE; 3.088 versus 3.307 mm h−1), while its correlation coefficient (CC) was higher (0.860 versus 0.832). Among the individual extensions, 3DEcho-QPENet had lower overall errors than 3DTime-QPENet. Their fusion, 3DHybrid-QPENet, achieved the lowest overall MAE (1.270 mm h−1) and RMSE (2.971 mm h−1), with a Bias of −0.537 mm h−1 and the highest CC (0.866). Across the baseline and extension comparisons, the time-resolved 3D representation and the joint temporal and multiscale configuration were associated with lower hourly QPE errors. 3DHybrid-QPENet also had the lowest relative error (RE), MAE, and RMSE in all five rainfall-intensity classes. Above 50 mm h−1, however, its Bias remained −20.031 mm h−1, indicating persistent underestimation. Generalization beyond the study region remains to be evaluated.

title: A Knowledge-Grounded AI Engine for Digital Twins: Supporting Conservation Through Long-Term Monitoring
summary: This paper presents a knowledge-grounded Digital Twin framework designed to support the interpretation of long-term structural monitoring data. The approach combines AI reasoning models, project-specific knowledge retrieval, numerical observations, and spatial information within an interactive environment where specialists can explore monitoring data and formulate analytical requests. The framework is demonstrated through the Milan Cathedral case study, using ground-based measurements, satellite interferometry data, and a selected subset of technical reports covering more than two decades. A Cesium-based 3D environment, including gaussian splatting visualization, provides spatial access to the monitoring information. The application illustrates how specialists can use AI to retrieve relevant knowledge, guide computational analyses, and examine relationships between monitoring observations and previous engineering interpretations. New forms of interaction among specialists, AI, and monitoring information are illustrated and discussed, highlighting the complementary roles of accumulated knowledge, AI-supported analysis, and human expertise in the interpretation process.

title: Elevation-Consistent 3D Gaussian Splatting for Few-View Satellite Photogrammetry
summary: Recovering 3D structure from multi-view satellite images is fundamental to urban planning, disaster assessment, and land monitoring. 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) offers an explicit geometric representation and real-time rendering, making it a promising alternative to stereo matching and neural radiance fields for satellite photogrammetry. Existing satellite 3DGS methods couple geometric optimization tightly with photometric signals. This coupling often leads to incomplete and overly smooth surfaces in vegetation and weak-texture regions. In this paper, we propose elevation-consistent 3D Gaussian splatting (ECGS), a method that breaks this coupling at the level of primitive creation and removal through three modules. First, we propose a multi-view elevation consistency regularization to establish cross-view geometric anchors, addressing elevation ambiguity without relying on photometric consistency. Second, a decoupled structure-aware densification mechanism is designed with an independent geometric pathway that keeps adding primitives where photometric gradients are unreliable. Finally, we introduce an importance-guided pruning strategy that removes the exposed redundancy through importance-weighted scores, while a geometric safety lock protects structural details. Experiments on the DFC2019 and IARPA 2016 benchmarks show that ECGS achieves better elevation estimates and higher-quality novel views. By jointly exploiting the radiometric appearance of multi-view imagery and the geometric evidence of cross-view correspondences, ECGS demonstrates that fusing these two modalities is an effective path toward intelligent remote sensing interpretation.

title: Evaluating the Timeliness of Tiled Object Detection in Satellite Videos: Effects of Result Release Frequency and Overlap Fusion
summary: Satellite video supports continuous vehicle monitoring, but processing delays can leave detections misaligned with current target positions. In tiled inference, release scheduling determines when regional detections become available, while overlap fusion combines them into a full-frame output. We develop a timeliness evaluation framework that matches available full-frame detections against query-time targets and tracks tile source frames and result availability. With detector weights fixed within each comparison, we evaluate release frequency, fusion, and construction cost through controlled replay and actual online execution. Fixed-lag experiments show that query-time quality generally declines as lag increases on VISO, SAT-MTB, and SDM-Car. Common-clock replay on SDM-Car shows that earlier regional release improves query-time matching with identical end-of-cycle detections. In online SDM-Car experiments with full-candidate fusion, batch-wise release at baseline load without motion prediction increased multi-frame DSFNet query-time F1 by 8.75% relative to end-of-cycle release. DSFNet benefited with causal motion prediction enabled; YOLOX-S benefited under increased processing load. Comparisons across fusion strategies and measured construction costs further showed that release gains depended on candidate retention and operating conditions. These findings support jointly selecting release frequency and overlap fusion while accounting for output construction cost.

title: QPAFusion: Query-Guided Radar Refinement and Prior-Guided Adaptive Fusion for Marine Object Detection
summary: Accurate marine target detection is essential for maritime situational awareness and safe navigation by unmanned surface vehicles. However, uneven radar returns and uncertain spatial correspondence complicate radar–camera fusion, while input-level integration does not explicitly adapt subsequent feature processing to local radar evidence. We propose QPAFusion, which refines multi-scale features through query-guided local radar sampling and adaptively aggregates feature branches using radar priors. On the WaterScenes dataset, QPAFusion achieves 64.5%mAP50−−95 and 90.9%mAP50, exceeding the reported three-frame REVP fusion baseline by 2.0 and 2.1 percentage points, respectively, with mAP50 gains of 6.4 and 3.1 percentage points on the adverse-lighting and adverse-weather subsets. These results support combining local-radar refinement with adaptive feature aggregation for object detection on the water surface, with larger accuracy gains on the evaluated adverse-condition subsets.

title: Distinguishing Slope-Wide Deformation Activity and Local Spatial Concentration in Reservoir Bank Slopes Using Time-Series InSAR
summary: Time-series interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) reveals spatially heterogeneous slope deformation, but a slope-wide statistic alone cannot describe the contribution of spatially clustered pixels with pronounced rates. We paired slope-wide deformation activity (ID), based on the mean and spatial dispersion of interval-specific line-of-sight (LOS) rates, with local spatial concentration (LSC), the threshold-weighted proportion of distribution-tail pixels assigned to spatial clusters. Both statistics were calculated for 116 adjacent-acquisition intervals from 117 ascending Sentinel-1A images of three Xiaowan Reservoir slopes. A five-class interpretation identified concurrent and divergent changes; transitional states accounted for 57–61 of the 115 intervals assigned to operational periods at each slope. During 22 April–4 May 2024, all three slopes reached their annual ID maxima. In the following interval, ID fell sharply while LSC remained relatively high. At Anlecun, the lower-tail contribution to LSC fell from 0.02548 to 0.00361 mm d−1, whereas the upper-tail contribution rose from 0.01298 to 0.03973 mm d−1. Thus, a high total LSC accompanied a substantial change in its tail composition. Pooled annual peak maps showed differences in clustered-pixel locations between selected peak and following intervals, providing spatial information that the LSC value alone does not retain. Together, the paired series, tail contributions, and maps can guide closer examination of intervals in which slope-wide activity and clustered-tail contributions differ. Inclinometers at Kongquedu provided limited directional consistency for stage-level changes.

title: Multitemporal Thermal Imaging for Archaeological Prospection
summary: Recent technological advances have made drone-based thermal imagery easier to acquire and process than ever before and a growing number of studies demonstrate the potential of aerial thermography to reveal archaeological landscape features. This paper brings together case studies at archaeological sites in New Mexico, Maine, and Oman where thermal imagery collected at different times in the diurnal cycle or under different environmental conditions displays cultural features with varying clarity. To leverage the potential of these multitemporal thermal image series, we experiment with several approaches to processing thermal imagery collected under different temperature and moisture conditions, the results of which can highlight subtle archaeological features and filter background noise. Despite ongoing challenges related to sensor data quality and the co-registration of thermal orthoimage mosaics, our results highlight the possibilities for advanced raster-based analyses of multitemporal thermal imagery to aid in archaeological prospection.

title: Physics-Aware Representation Learning Framework for Cross-Parameter Ground Penetrating Radar Inversion
summary: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) inversion using deep learning may experience substantial performance degradation when acquisition parameters differ between training and testing. One important factor contributing to this sensitivity is the conventional use of raw time-domain representations, in which information associated with different frequency bands, propagation scales, and phase characteristics is implicitly mixed. To address this problem, we propose a token-enhanced Transformer–mixture-of-experts (MoE) U-Net (TET-MoE), a physics-aware representation-learning framework that integrates three complementary components: multiscale wavelet-plus-phase tokenization for structured signal representation, lightweight Transformer blocks for global cross-scale dependency modeling, and a convolutional MoE module with sparse dynamic routing for adaptive feature processing at the bottleneck. The pretraining–encoder-freezing–decoder-fine-tuning strategy adapts the model to 200 MHz, a target frequency omitted from pretraining and within the 80–300 MHz span of the six source frequencies. The 200 MHz fine-tuning inputs amount to less than 1% of the source-domain training inputs. TET-MoE outperforms the baseline U-Net under matched fine-tuning conditions at 200 MHz. Ablation studies, noise tests, and auxiliary classification further evaluate the model. For field inference, the source-pretrained model was fine-tuned on synthetic 110 MHz data and then applied to field data collected with a nominal 100 MHz antenna. The results indicate that the proposed design improves inversion accuracy, convergence behavior, and structural fidelity under the evaluated conditions.

title: Geometry-Aware Supervision for Connectivity-Preserving Road Extraction via SAM2
summary: Road extraction from remote sensing imagery is a structured problem: a mask with high region overlap may still contain breaks that make the road network unusable, and the difficulty grows when annotated sources are small, heterogeneous, and unequally represented during joint training. We revisit this problem on a SAM2 encoder while keeping all added complexity in training rather than in the deployed network. First, we do not use SAM2 as a black box: its top-down pathway refines only the coarsest levels, leaving the quarter-resolution features our decoder needs semantically shallow, so a feature-enhancement neck restores the missing top-down path and a directional attention module matches the elongated geometry of roads. Second, we decompose road structure into five complementary geometric views—skeleton, direction, width, neighbourhood affinity, and endpoints—used as a shared training-time prior; each is a deterministic function of the segmentation mask, so the prior needs no extra annotation and no learned generator, and its heads are removed after training, leaving the inference graph free of auxiliary computation; the feature-enhancement neck and directional attention module remain in the deployed model, as they serve the segmentation head. A soft-clDice term supervises centrelines, and a square-root sampler rebalances the 5.2:1 update-frequency skew across sources. On Massachusetts, DeepGlobe, and CHN6-CUG, the model reaches an aggregate IoU of 0.7403 and CC-agreement of 0.6874, improving CC-agreement by 44% over D-LinkNet and 10% over the strongest same-backbone adaptation. We also make evaluation part of the contribution: we measure an empirical uncertainty scale for topology metrics and hold every claim to exceed it. Held to this standard, the prior’s CC-agreement gain clears the scale only in the scarce-annotation regime that limits operational mapping yet costs nothing to retain elsewhere. Finally, region overlap and CC-agreement rank models differently, so both metric families should be reported against a stated measurement scale.

title: PINF-RCAF for Trust-Guided Residual Alignment in Bi-Temporal Building Change Detection
summary: Local displacement, illumination changes, and repeated roof textures can produce false building changes in bi-temporal remote-sensing images. We propose PINF-RCAF to detect change from the discrepancy that remains after local transport and nuisance regression. The Pseudo-Invariant Nuisance Field (PINF) estimates displacement-penalized bidirectional transport, and Pseudo-Invariant Residual Regression (PIRR) removes the locally explained component. Reciprocal Correlation Alignment Fusion (RCAF) combines local correlation, forward–backward cycle agreement, and learned trust to control semantic and boundary corrections. A direct residual path to the decoder preserves evidence for structures without a reliable temporal counterpart. At a fixed threshold of 0.50, three independently seeded training runs yield mean test F1/IoU of 0.9305/0.8701 on FOTBCD, 0.9448/0.8954 on LEVIR-CD, and 0.9722/0.9460 on DSIFN-CD. The mean F1 gains over the matched Control are 3.49, 2.58, and 1.26 percentage points, respectively. Component comparisons identify the gains from local matching and residual correction. Boundary evaluation and controlled validation-set appearance perturbations further show improved contour placement and fewer background responses. These results support the use of correspondence reliability to refine residual change evidence.

title: LSUR: Local Statistical and Uncertainty-Guided Refinement for Infrared Small Target Detection
summary: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) requires the preservation of extremely weak target responses while suppressing structured background clutter. Existing detectors have substantially improved feature representation, yet two issues remain common across architectures: shallow features are usually processed without explicitly measuring local statistical distinctiveness, and high-resolution details are often fused uniformly without considering the reliability of the current prediction. To address these issues, we propose LSUR, a lightweight plug-and-play refinement framework composed of multi-scale local statistical enhancement (MLSE) and confidence–uncertainty-guided refinement (CUGR). MLSE measures the standardized deviation of shallow feature responses within multiple local neighborhoods and adaptively integrates the resulting statistical responses, thereby enhancing locally distinctive target cues with varying background contrast. CUGR derives target-confidence and uncertainty maps from the base prediction and uses them to selectively retrieve high-resolution information for residual logit refinement. The framework requires only one shallow feature, the prediction feature, and the base output, allowing it to be attached to different encoder–decoder IRSTD detectors. Extensive experiments on three public IRSTD datasets and multiple representative detectors demonstrate that LSUR consistently improves detection performance with limited additional computational cost. Specifically, integrating LSUR with SCTransNet improves IoU by 1.68, 0.73, and 1.44 percentage points on NUAA-SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1K, respectively. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of local statistical modeling, multi-scale aggregation, and confidence–uncertainty-guided refinement.

title: DS-UNet: A Fine-Grained Highway Region Segmentation Model from UAV Perspective
summary: Accurate highway region segmentation is essential for road inspection and traffic scene understanding. However, complex backgrounds, viewpoint variations, occlusions and shadows often lead to incomplete segmentation of road regions and inaccurate boundary predictions. This paper proposes an improved UNet model, DS-UNet, for fine-grained highway region segmentation from UAV imagery. A Dilated-Global Context Block (DGCBlock) is embedded within the encoder to fuse multi-scale dilated features with global context information, enhancing the feature representation of continuous road structures. Meanwhile, a Semantic-Guided Channel-Spatial Attention (SGCSA) module is devised for the decoder, in which high-level semantic features guide channel-spatial feature recalibration to boost fine-detail reconstruction and suppress background interference. In addition, a boundary-weighted BCE-Dice hybrid loss (BWD) is proposed to strengthen supervision for road boundary pixels. To evaluate the model’s performance, this paper constructed the UAVRR3K dataset consisting of 3000 highway region images captured under diverse UAV perspectives and complex road scenarios. Experimental results show that DS-UNet achieves an F1 of 97.31% and a Road-class IoU of 94.76%, outperforming comparative models. Benefiting from the proposed BWD loss, boundary recall reaches 77.88%. These results verify that our method effectively enhances road region integrity and boundary completeness, offering reliable technical support for UAV-based intelligent highway inspection.

title: DPNMS: A Density-Peak-Based Non-Maximum Suppression Algorithm for High-Quality Oriented Object Detection
summary: Aerial imagery objects present characteristics such as arbitrary orientations, dense distribution, and a wide range of scales. Mainstream detectors add angles to traditional rectangular bounding boxes to better fit the object boundaries, but this makes the detection task even more challenging. Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) is a filter designed to address duplicate detections in dense detectors, extracting the most representative output from multiple detection results for a single object. However, the NMS algorithm has fundamental problems, including the risk of wrong suppression due to confidence-based prioritization, poor computational speed from sequential processing, and inefficient use of its output data. To address the above challenges, and based on the data patterns of objects in remote sensing imagery, we reviewed NMS as a local density peak clustering task and proposed a novel post-processing method called DPNMS. We integrated information across each output through statistical analysis to construct its density representations, and then searched for peak values within valid neighborhoods defined by the IoU threshold. To prevent suppressing effective boxes, we designed a “select–release” cyclic workflow to correct the chosen result. The proposed method integrates the detector’s output information to achieve competitive results. Our method does not require sorting the localization information in reverse order of confidence, and each operation is independent of the others, allowing for parallelization and resulting in high computational efficiency. Extensive experiments conducted on various datasets and multiple platforms have validated the effectiveness and stability of the proposed method. The unique filtering strategy offers a new framework for post-processing methods in remote sensing image object detection.

title: Observability of Vegetation Responses to Tropical Cyclones in Southern Africa Using Solar-Induced Fluorescence and Normalised Difference Vegetation Index
summary: Satellite assessments of vegetation responses to tropical cyclones depend on both indicator sensitivity and observational availability. We evaluated 21 storm-country study areas in Southern Africa from 2018 to 2021 using TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) as a photosynthesis-linked indicator and Aqua Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) normalised difference vegetation index (NDVI) as an independent measure of canopy greenness. Storm-week responses within 200 km of cyclone tracks were estimated using spatial-block bootstrap intervals. Usable storm-week SIF was available for 12 study areas (nested within seven cyclones), whereas NDVI was available for all 21. Across the 12 matched study areas, SIF changes ranged from −42.9% to +35.5% and NDVI changes from −4.0% to +6.1%. The +35.5% Desmond extreme represents storm-week SIF remaining above the pre-storm baseline while a pre-existing greening trajectory was interrupted, not cyclone-enhanced photosynthesis; the −42.9% Chalane–Zimbabwe extreme is based on two usable SIF days and is interpreted cautiously. At the study-area level, the indicators agreed in two cases, opposed one another in three, and were statistically unresolved in seven because at least one interval included zero; these 2/3/7 counts do not represent independent cyclone events. Diane, Francisco, and Kenneth showed SIF decreases alongside NDVI increases, demonstrating that greenness did not reproduce the direction of the photosynthesis-linked response. NDVI generally returned to its seasonal range earlier than SIF. These findings show that SIF and NDVI provide complementary but non-equivalent evidence and that sparse SIF sampling determines which cyclone responses can be distinguished from no change.

title: Detection of Freshwater Water-Clear-of-Ice Timing During Break-Up Using SWOT KaRIn Pixel Cloud Data: A Case Study at Lhù’ààn Mǟn (Kluane Lake), Yukon
summary: Following the launch of the Surface Water Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission, data collected during the calibration/validation “fast sampling” phase were acquired daily for select swaths, presenting a unique opportunity to monitor ice break-up for Lhù’ààn Mǟn (Kluane Lake, Yukon Territory, Canada) using the Ka-band Radar Interferometer (KaRIn). The KaRIn pixel cloud product is designed to provide backscatter and surface elevation for open water; however, it effectively discriminates ice-covered regions on the lake. In this study, the efficacy of the KaRIn pixel cloud product is evaluated for the retrieval of the timing of water-clear-of-ice (WCI), an ice phenology parameter that has proven difficult to resolve using co- or cross-polarized synthetic aperture radar. The Dynamic Threshold Variability Method (DTVM) is evaluated against optical remote sensing from near-daily PlanetScope acquisitions, and is also within the physically plausible range of lake-wide melt out dates simulated by the one-dimensional thermodynamic Canadian Lake Ice Model (CLIMo). At 11 Points of Interest (POIs), SWOT observed the transition from break-up to water-clear-of-ice phase from 23 May 2023 to 30 May 2023, a total of 8 days, with an RMSE of 1.2 days (95% confidence interval of 0.6–1.7 days), and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.8 days (95% confidence interval of 0.4–1 days) for WCI derived using the Dynamic Threshold Variability Method (DTVM) at a tessellated resolution of 100 m. When comparing PlanetScope WCI to the DTVM using the 50th percentile of thresholds for all 100 m tessellation pixels across the lake, the RMSE is 8.69 days, with an MAE of 3.15 days. While SWOT has since transitioned to the science phase (21-day repeat pass), the use of KaRIn during the fast sampling phase to retrieve WCI presents the opportunity to discriminate between melting freshwater ice and open water during the break-up season that previous SAR observations have had difficulty resolving.

title: Integrating AlphaEarth Satellite Embeddings and Natural Language GeoAI for Traceable Forest Change Monitoring in South Korea
summary: Annual satellite embeddings offer reusable features for forest monitoring, while administrative applications require clear reference definitions and traceable reporting. We evaluated AlphaEarth (AE) features against transitions between the 2019 and 2025 forest type maps of Chuncheon, Korea, and integrated satellite and map-based analyses in a natural-language decision support service. Four map-derived classes supplied 6027 stratified points partitioned using 5 km spatial blocks. In the endpoint-year comparison on 1084 held-out points, binary change-detection F1 was 0.926 for AE, 0.772 for the Sentinel-2 (S2) normalized difference vegetation index and normalized burn ratio, and 0.811 for four S2 indices. For the 2019–2025 annual window, F1 was 0.933 for AE, 0.887 for Sentinel-2 indices and 0.896 when locally pretrained representation features were added. Matching nominal windows left differences in sensor inputs, pretraining, feature dimensionality, spatial support and annual product construction. Conditional change-type macro-F1 was 0.777, with the lowest class F1 for conversion (0.621). Forest-gain labels predominantly identified transitions from mapped unstocked land to mapped tree cover. AE peaks fell within one year of 77.4% of 31 recorded management operations using the 2018–2025 search and 67.7% using the 2020–2025 search. Map-derived hotspots contained 267.7 ha of harvest/regeneration and conversion. The Chuncheon AE + S2 classifier achieved F1 = 0.831 at threshold 0.5 in nearby Inje County without retraining. All 973 checked numerical tokens matched tool outputs in 14 saved reports, including two language-agent reports. This audit covered numerical correspondence in the saved outputs. The framework supports candidate selection for forest inspection. Wider use requires independent reference validation and transfer tests beyond Inje.

title: A Cross-Sensor Comparison of Multi-View Hyperspectral 3D Reconstruction and Multispectral Laser Scanning for Spatially Resolved Lettuce Disease Assessment
summary: The joint interpretation of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) and laser-based 3D observations is challenged by differences in surface sampling, acquisition geometry, and spectral response. This proof-of-concept study evaluated internal spectral consistency and cross-sensor correspondence in independently generated 3D plant representations. We developed an accessible CPU-based workflow for dense, spectrally attributed 3D reconstructions of healthy and Sclerotinia sclerotiorum-infected lettuce plants (Lactuca sativa var. longifolia typ. Romana and var. capitata typ. Canasta) using multi-view VNIR push-broom HSI (204 bands, 400–1000 nm). The resulting models were compared with independently acquired PlantEye (PE) multispectral 3D laser scans using an external reference for registration. A view-selection policy for spectral attribution reduced raw reflectance dispersion by ~64%, achieving 98.7–99.5% canopy spectral assignment coverage and high spatial specificity (median contributing views SAM: 1.68–2.37°). While differences in acquisition geometry precluded point-wise sensor equivalence, both modalities effectively discriminated inoculated from non-inoculated leaves within each plant using four common spectral bands via spatially grouped cross-validation (balanced accuracy: 0.923–0.930 for ‘Canasta’; 0.824–0.866 for ‘Romana’). Furthermore, full 204-band HSI models yielded improved tissue discrimination. The results highlight the need to distinguish internal spectral consistency, local cross-sensor correspondence, and task-level information when evaluating heterogeneous spectral–3D observations for future joint use.
