title: Cross-Calibration of the TROPICS Pathfinder W-Band Radiometer with the GPM Microwave Imager
summary: The objective of this paper is to describe a robust technique to perform the inter-satellite radiometric calibration (XCAL) between two microwave radiometers of significantly different designs. Because this results in the relative calibration between the two, one is the reference and the other is the to-be-calibrated target. This technique makes no judgment as to which is the best absolute calibration; rather, it only considers the relative difference between the two. For our application, the Global Precipitation Measurement Microwave Imager (GMI) is the transfer standard for the inter-satellite radiometric calibration of a constellation of cooperative satellites’ microwave radiometers used to provide global precipitation measurements for an international community of scientific and operational users. This paper describes the on-orbit validation process for a future candidate GPM constellation member, namely, the 91.6-GHz TROPICS Pathfinder radiometer. A one-year TROPICS–GMI matchup dataset was developed using spatially and temporally collocated brightness temperature observations over clear-sky ocean scenes. Also, these brightness temperature data were combined with estimates of the associated environmental parameters, provided by a global numerical weather model product. The associated XCAL analysis procedures are described, and the radiometric bias results are presented.

title: HiMoTrack: Small-Object Perception and Hierarchical Motion Recovery for UAV Multi-Object Tracking
summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based multi-object tracking (MOT) is important for intelligent traffic analysis but remains challenging because small object scales, frequent occlusions, motion blur, and changing aerial viewpoints jointly degrade detection quality and trajectory continuity. This paper presents HiMoTrack, a tracking-by-detection framework that addresses this degradation chain by improving small-object observations and progressively recovering low-quality tracks. Specifically, a Small Object Feature Efficient Perception Network (SOFEPNet) preserves spatial detail and reconstructs multi-scale features for aerial small objects. For motion recovery, a Velocity Adaptive Cubature Kalman Filter (VACKF) provides reliability-adaptive short-term state estimation, while a Group Motion Compensation Strategy (GMCS) exploits local group-motion consistency when individual observations become unreliable. When no reliable neighboring motion prior is available, Spatio-Temporal Memory Prediction (STMP) uses historical trajectory memory to infer the missing state and maintain temporal continuity. In this way, the detector, motion estimator, and trajectory recovery process are organized around the same objective: stabilizing weak and interrupted trajectories in complex UAV traffic scenes. Experiments show that HiMoTrack achieves multi-object tracking accuracy (MOTA) scores of 64.6% on the UAVDT benchmark and 62.4% on VisDrone while maintaining strong overall tracking accuracy and competitive trajectory continuity. Additional experiments on MOT17 demonstrate that the proposed motion recovery strategy can be integrated into representative trackers, indicating good modularity and transferability.

title: RS-DeCLIP: Gated Dual-Source DeCLIP Adaptation with Side-Branch Query-Based Local Fusion for Remote Sensing Image–Text Retrieval
summary: Remote sensing image–text retrieval requires diverse textual supervision and fine-grained visual representations. Redundant captions limit linguistic diversity, while rewriting can introduce semantic drift. A single global image descriptor may also underrepresent small objects and local spatial arrangements, limiting fine-grained discrimination. To address these challenges, we propose RS-DeCLIP, a two-stage retrieval framework. Stage 1 adapts a RemoteCLIP ViT-B/32 dual encoder with DeCLIP-style multi-view supervision using official captions and captions polished by a large language model. A semantic consistency gate downweights text self-supervision (TSS) between less consistent original and rewritten captions. Similarity-aware negative downweighting and text-to-image weighting address ambiguous negatives and directional imbalance, while training-only fine-grained alignment strengthens detail sensitivity. Stage 2 targets the fine-grained visual information underrepresented by the global descriptor. Five learnable visual query vectors, conditioned on the global image embedding and guided by soft spatial preferences, attend to a dense P2 feature map to extract local evidence. Consistency-gated orthogonal residual fusion integrates this evidence into the frozen global image embedding. These visual queries are distinct from the user’s text query: image feature extraction and fusion do not use the retrieval text, so fused image descriptors can be precomputed and compared with independently encoded text vectors. On the Remote Sensing Image Captioning Dataset (RSICD), Stage 1 improves mean recall (MR) from 35.26% to 38.54%, and Stage 2 further increases MR to 39.27%. On the Remote Sensing Image–Text Match Dataset (RSITMD), Stage 2 improves MR from 50.90% to 52.58%. The final model exceeds the reported GeoRSCLIP-FT (RET-2) results by 0.40 and 0.77 percentage points on RSICD and RSITMD, respectively, and the Representation Discrepancy Bridging (RDB) method by 1.18 and 0.54 percentage points.

title: A Climate-Responsive Weighted Ensemble for Rapeseed Yield Estimation Across the Middle and Lower Reaches of the Yangtze River
summary: Regional winter rapeseed yield prediction requires models that remain reliable across highly variable climate conditions. We developed an interpretable climate-responsive ensemble for rapeseed yield prediction using satellite and environmental predictors. The framework was evaluated on 542 city–year observations from 73 cities in the middle and lower Yangtze River from 2014 to 2022. Monthly Landsat vegetation indices and TerraClimate variables were screened using Group Lasso. We evaluated three base learners using leave-one-year-out cross-validation: a temporal convolutional network (TCN), a bidirectional long short-term memory network, and a random forest. We combined their predictions using regime-specific weights. The ensemble achieved a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.848, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 189 kg ha−1, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 151 kg ha−1 and a relative RMSE of 8.9%. Compared with the TCN, the strongest base learner overall, it reduced RMSE by 25.57 kg ha−1 under waterlogging and 8.98 kg ha−1 under combined freeze and waterlogging. SHapley Additive exPlanations of the random-forest component identified spring vegetation indices and soil moisture as the strongest predictors, with soil moisture more influential under waterlogging and drought–waterlogging. Climate-anomaly context was associated with changes in model skill and predictor attribution, supporting regional rapeseed yield monitoring under contrasting meteorological conditions.

title: Mining-Induced Surface Deformation Monitoring and Short-Term Prediction Using DS-InSAR and Increment-Target Spatiotemporal Learning
summary: Mining-induced subsidence is a common geological hazard in coal mining areas, and reliable deformation monitoring is important for risk reduction. Cumulative InSAR deformation fields contain deformation accumulated during preceding periods, whereas newly occurring deformation over a short forecast horizon generally represents only a small fraction of the cumulative magnitude. Direct prediction of future cumulative deformation may therefore exploit temporal persistence to achieve relatively low mean errors while underestimating locally strong subsidence. To investigate this issue, we used 276 ascending Sentinel-1 SAR images acquired from 10 January 2020 to 11 July 2024 to perform DS-InSAR monitoring at the Wutongzhuang Mine, Hebei Province, China, and constructed 138 continuous two-dimensional cumulative vertical deformation fields. We defined three prediction tasks—cumulative-input–cumulative-output (C2C), cumulative-input–increment-output (C2D), and increment-input–increment-output (D2D)—and applied each task to CNN-PhLSTM, ConvLSTM, and VMRNN. Monitoring identified two major subsidence zones in the north-central and southwestern parts of the study area, with a maximum cumulative vertical deformation of approximately −467.96mm by 11 July 2024. The Pearson correlation of colocated PS-InSAR and DS-InSAR deformation rates was 0.88; comparison between DS-InSAR and leveling at P1 and P2 yielded a correlation of 0.9742, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 8.23 mm, and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 10.29 mm. Keeping historical cumulative deformation inputs unchanged and converting the future supervision target to deformation increments reduced the RMSEs of CNN-PhLSTM, ConvLSTM, and VMRNN by 56.48%, 12.17%, and 17.16%, respectively, with consistent improvement directions across three random seeds. Further converting historical inputs to increments produced smaller, model-dependent changes. Under the unified D2D task, VMRNN achieved the lowest mean RMSE and MAE and the highest mean R2, showing relatively favorable overall predictive performance among the compared models. Spatial predictions also show that VMRNN-D2D generally preserves the spatial structures of the major subsidence zones and local troughs, while errors are concentrated mainly in actively developing strong-subsidence areas, where subsidence magnitudes tend to be underestimated. These findings indicate that representing the future supervision target as deformation increments provides an effective strategy for improving short-term prediction of cumulative InSAR deformation across different networks.

title: Ionospheric and Geomagnetic Effects of the X5.8 Solar Flare on 11 May 2024
summary: An X5.8-class solar flare began at 01:10 UT on 11 May 2024, during the main phase of the super geomagnetic storm, providing an opportunity to investigate solar flare effects under highly disturbed space weather conditions. Using multi-instrument observations from the Sanya incoherent scatter radar (ISR), ionosondes, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers, and ground magnetometers, this study investigates the ionospheric and geomagnetic responses over East Asia. The Sanya ISR observations revealed pronounced electron density enhancements near 110 km and at 300–400 km, with electron density at 300–400 km reaching 1.92–4.08 times the background values. The F2-layer peak electron density (NmF2) increased rapidly to 2.02 × 1012 el/m3, approximately three times its preflare value, whereas the F2-layer peak height (hmF2) initially decreased and subsequently increased. The ISR-derived vertical total electron content (TEC) increased by approximately 20 TECU relative to the reference day, with the fractional contribution from around 350 km increasing by approximately 5 percentage points. Ionosonde observations revealed pronounced latitudinal differences. F-region echoes at Mohe and Beijing nearly disappeared against the background of a strong negative ionospheric storm, whereas the flare-associated response was more prominent at the low-latitude station Sanya, where the minimum reflection frequency (fmin) increased to 8.85–9.95 MHz. GNSS-TEC observations revealed distinct latitudinal differences in the ionospheric response, with maximum TEC enhancements of 36.76 and 35.40 TECU at the low-latitude stations SYBG and QION, respectively. At middle latitudes, the negative ionospheric storm remained dominant despite short-term positive flare-associated enhancements, while some stations in the northeastern high-latitude region exhibited small positive perturbations superimposed on the negative background. The geomagnetic response exhibited a pronounced east–west asymmetry within the 40–50°N latitude band, with positive disturbances in the horizontal component of the geomagnetic field over 75–95°E and negative disturbances over 96–135°E. These findings suggest that flare-induced photoionization and conductivity enhancement interacted with the pre-existing storm-time electrodynamic environment, producing altitude-dependent ionospheric responses and pronounced spatial variations in TEC and geomagnetic disturbances.

title: Decoupling Ecological Trends from Stochastic Climate Volatility: Spatiotemporal Transitions and Future Resilience in Arid and Semi-Arid Regions
summary: Arid ecosystems face severe climate threats, yet stochastic climate volatility often masks true ecological transitions. In this study, we developed an integrated spatiotemporal framework to decouple mean ecological trends from climate noise in Gansu Province, China. We combined Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) time series, the multi-scalar Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), and a probabilistic Dust Hazard Index (DHI) to evaluate historical dynamics (2001–2024). Subsequently, eco-environmental sustainability (2025–2099) was projected under CMIP6 scenarios using a Random Forest algorithm optimized via spatial block cross-validation. Historical evaluations revealed a significant regional ecological amelioration (RSEI trend: +0.0279/decade, p < 0.01), with the degraded area decreasing from 68.60% in 2001 to 52.68% in 2024. However, spatial polarization persisted, with severe degradation covering 38.84% of the hyper-arid northwest. Feature importance and dual correlation analyses identified short-term moisture deficits (SPEI-3) and chronic dust exposure as primary biophysical controls; notably, dust hazards strongly suppressed vegetation in degraded zones (r = −0.43). Future projections indicate that warming-induced aridity will intensify ecological stress. Under the intermediate SSP2-4.5 scenario, the area of Serious Decline (SSD) expands from 35.09% in the near term to 47.15% by the end of the century. Conversely, the high-emission SSP5-8.5 scenario, characterized by thermal extremes up to 3.58 °C, triggers an abrupt structural transition during 2061–2099; the SSD area more than triples (from 12.13% to 43.95%), overwhelming historical restoration gains. Safeguarding these fragile drylands necessitates proactive management integrating targeted dust mitigation and water rights allocation.

title: LightMaskMamba: A Near-Ground Remote Sensing Object Detection Network with Visible–Infrared Fusion
summary: Visible–infrared fusion is a main route to all-weather object extraction in near-ground remote sensing, but single-band RGB remains unstable under occlusion, clutter, and low light and illumination variation. This study presents LightMaskMamba, a lightweight visible–infrared object detection network for near-ground remote sensing. Public benchmarks test fusion quality across scenes, and the self-built near-ground wampee field dataset is for deployment-oriented field validation. The core of the network is a lightweight mask-guided Mamba fusion architecture. Its key module, the Lightweight Mask Mamba Fusion Block (LMMFB), uses an object-related mask to drive shallow-to-deep VIS–NIR feature fusion, focuses computation on object regions, and reduces scan redundancy. Dual-band detection therefore stays light enough to run at the edge. On the self-built wampee dataset, LightMaskMamba-v11s reaches 97.4% mAP50 and 52.0% mAP50:95. Relative to single-band YOLOv11s, mAP50 is 2.3 and 4.6 percentage points higher on IR and RGB. Parameters rise by 3.7M, from 8.8M to 12.5M. The same model is likewise effective in detection accuracy, and lighter, on public multimodal object-detection datasets. On a Jetson Orin NX Super, TensorRT INT8 mixed-precision inference reaches about 17.3 FPS, or 58 ms per image.

title: BCTBM: A Bottom-Current-Fused Two-Stage BM-mRMR Method for Seafloor Sediment Classification
summary: Seafloor sediment classification is critical for benthic habitat mapping and marine environmental protection. Existing classification methods mostly adopt seafloor surface observation parameters such as backscatter and bathymetry. These parameters only characterize surface seabed properties and lack physical prior information related to sediment formation mechanisms, which limits classification accuracy and physical interpretability. Considering that bottom-current kinetic energy (BCKE) governs sediment erosion, transport and deposition and further shapes the spatial distribution of sediments, this paper proposes a bottom-current-fused two-stage Bayesian MIC-augmented mRMR (BCTBM) architecture for seafloor sediment classification. BCTBM combines BCKE with acoustic and topographic features to construct a 77-dimensional multi-source feature set. Samples with high class separability are selected using the Jeffries–Matusita (J-M) distance, and a two-stage feature selection algorithm is further developed. ReliefF is first applied for coarse-grained feature screening to generate a candidate feature set; subsequently, the Bayesian MIC-augmented Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (BM-mRMR) model employs Bayesian optimization (BO) to adaptively solve the optimal relevance–redundancy trade-off weights for seven target dimensions, and mRMR finally derives the optimal feature set based on the obtained optimal weights. The proposed method is validated in the shallow-water sediment classification scenario of the eastern English Channel. Eighty-four comparative experiments demonstrate that introducing BCKE improves the overall accuracy by 3.48% on average, with a maximum increment of 9.4%. The proposed two-stage BM-mRMR method achieves average accuracy improvements of 4.84% and 6.08% over ReliefF and ReliefF-mRMR, respectively. The classification results are consistent with the Hjulström–Sundborg sedimentary-dynamic framework, offering an effective pathway for refined benthic habitat mapping.

title: STELLA: A Connectivity Representation for Lane Marking Detection from Satellite Imagery
summary: High-definition (HD) maps for autonomous driving store each lane marking as a separate polyline. Satellite imagery covers wide areas at low cost, but current methods cannot turn it directly into such polylines. The reason is that no existing output representation suits polyline detection. Segmentation masks do not tell which line a pixel belongs to, and they merge lines that meet or cross. Existing cell-wise connectivity representations tie their output slots to fixed angular sectors. Their training target therefore changes discontinuously at sector boundaries. We propose STELLA, an output representation suited to polylines, and a method to train it. At each grid cell, STELLA predicts one self-slot and two unordered connection slots. During training, these slots are matched to the ground-truth (GT) connections at minimum cost. One line thus becomes one chain of cells, and post-processing only cleans up overlapping lines. We also propose AI-CCQ, an asymmetric instance-level metric for thin, long lines. It gives credit to a partly drawn line but rejects a line that switches to a neighboring marking. On the SEED-MAP test set, STELLA reaches an AI-CCQ F1 score of 0.4483, against 0.3005 for a segmentation-based method and 0.3551 for the Sat2Graph representation.

title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for RGB Surface-Landmine Detection: Sequence-Held-Out Evaluation on SULAND_v2
summary: Domain shift remains a challenge for RGB-based surface-landmine detection, particularly when labeled imagery from a new environment is unavailable. This study examines unsupervised domain adaptation on SULAND_v2 using YOLOv8-S and a teacher–student framework. Complete acquisition sequences are separated between adaptation and evaluation, and seven adaptation configurations are compared across three source-training seeds. On the primary assignment, mean average precision at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.50 (mAP50) increases from 53.70% for the source-only model to 63.56% for Mean Teacher and 64.22% for the CMT-style configuration. Controls with the same optimization budget indicate that additional training alone does not account for the Mean Teacher improvement. The pooled gain is concentrated in PMA-2, whereas PFM-1 performance decreases. Reversing the adaptation and evaluation sequences yields improvements for both classes, suggesting that the class response depends on the sequence assignment. Individual-sequence results and class-specific recall and false positives further reveal variation within the pooled scores. Additional alignment objectives provide small, inconsistent gains over Mean Teacher on the primary assignment, while source-domain accuracy decreases modestly. These findings suggest that unlabeled target imagery can improve detection within the evaluated dataset, although its benefits vary across classes and acquisitions. The intended application is candidate generation for visible surface targets and analyst review; operational reliability requires further validation.

title: Mapping Gross Primary Productivity of Sunlit and Shaded Leaves at 30 m in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region Using a Seasonal, Vegetation-Type-Specific Clumping Index
summary: Accurate estimation of gross primary productivity (GPP) at fine spatial and temporal resolutions is essential for characterizing carbon uptake across heterogeneous landscapes. Coarse-resolution GPP products smooth differences among neighboring vegetation patches, while many fine-resolution products report only total GPP and do not distinguish the contributions of sunlit and shaded leaves. In this study, we developed SS-GPP30, a spatially continuous dataset that provides 8-day estimates of total GPP and its sunlit- and shaded-leaf components at 30 m resolution across the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region from 2017 to 2025. The dataset was generated using a two-leaf light-use-efficiency framework driven by Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS)-derived leaf area index, regional-scale ERA5 meteorological forcing (0.25°), annual 30 m land cover, and seasonal, vegetation-type-specific dynamic representative clumping index. The methodological advance over existing high-resolution GPP products lies in integrating 30 m HLS-based canopy dynamics with sunlit–shaded TL-LUE modeling and seasonal vegetation-type-specific dynamic clumping index, thereby enabling finer temporal representation of canopy photosynthesis and spatial characterization of heterogeneous landscapes. Evaluation against flux-derived GPP at eight eddy covariance sites showed that the seasonal index reduced the root-mean-square error in four of five vegetation and crop groups, with the largest reductions in forest (5.3%) and shrubland (4.6%). Cross-product comparisons across vegetation types yielded R2 values ranging from 0.70 to 0.89, while SS-GPP30 better preserved fine-scale spatial heterogeneity than coarser-resolution products. During 2017–2025, mean annual GPP was 1431.7 g C m−2 yr−1, with sunlit- and shaded-leaf GPP contributing 742.0 and 689.7 g C m−2 yr−1, respectively. Shaded leaves contributed 48.2% of total GPP and showed marked spatiotemporal variation. Both components increased significantly, with a stronger trend in shaded-leaf GPP. Therefore, SS-GPP30 fills an important gap in fine-resolution GPP mapping by providing 30 m estimates of total, sunlit-leaf, and shaded-leaf GPP, thereby resolving both regional vegetation productivity and within-canopy photosynthetic partitioning across the BTH region. The framework also has potential for application to other regions.

title: A Robust Method for Tiny-Target Detection in Deep-Space Images by Integrating Physical Laws with Deep Learning
summary: This paper proposes a Noise-Decoupled Multi-scale Evidence-aware (NDME) algorithm to address the critical challenges of feature sparsity and noise interference in detecting tiny targets (occupying <0.1% of image area) in deep-space images. By innovatively integrating physical principles with deep learning, NDME constructs a Multi-scale Quantized Feature Pyramid Network (MS-QFPN) and introduces a Non-local Sub-pixel Attention (NSA) mechanism to effectively enhance the sparse feature representation of tiny targets. Simultaneously, an adaptive noise-signal covariance matrix based on the International Celestial Reference Frame 3 (ICRF-3)-inspired deep-space noise physical model is designed to suppress cosmic-ray noise while preserving weak target features (signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) > 2). Compared with state-of-the-art methods such as YOLOX series and ALCNet, NDME demonstrates significant advantages in small-target detection on the IST-S and IRDST datasets, exhibiting robust adaptability under complex noise environments. Experimental results show that NDME outperforms existing methods in recall, precision, and other key metrics, providing an effective solution for tiny-target detection under deep-space-like sparse-feature and noise conditions, while validation on real deep-space observations remains future work. It should be noted that the public benchmarks used in this work are deep-space-like infrared proxy datasets; they are used to evaluate the sparse-feature and noise-robustness aspects of the method rather than to claim direct deep-space validation.

title: RADAR: Glass-Induced Reflection Artifact Detection and Removal for Terrestrial Laser Scanning
summary: Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) is pivotal for creating high-precision 3D geospatial data in urban digital twins and Scan-to-BIM applications. However, TLS point clouds frequently suffer from severe glass-induced reflection artifacts, which fundamentally compromise geometric fidelity and downstream automated modeling. Existing methods struggle with real-world physical complexities because they rely heavily on idealized reflection symmetry assumptions and fail to address the critical “measurement void” problem caused by transparent surfaces. To address these limitations, we propose a unified cross-modal framework RADAR for robust reflection artifact removal in complex urban environments. First, our approach leverages a multimodal vision foundation model—integrating panoramic imagery and LiDAR-derived spatial maps—to accurately detect glass regions. These initial masks are then geometrically refined and completed via ray-casting to recover missing surfaces. Second, to handle imperfect reflections, we introduce the Reflection-aware Local–Global Geometric Similarity (RE-LGGS) descriptor. By jointly encoding multi-scale PCA-derived structures and spatial orientation consistency, RE-LGGS robustly identifies virtual points even under severe geometric distortion and data sparsity. Extensive evaluations on multiple public TLS datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves competitive performance across diverse glass-scene conditions.

title: Estimation of Theoretical Maize Straw Resources and Evaluation of Utilization Potential in West-Central Jilin, China, Using the CASA Model on the Google Earth Engine Platform
summary: Rapid and accurate assessment of maize straw volume and spatial distribution can help to improve straw utilization efficiency. This study estimated the theoretical maize straw resources of West-Central Jilin Province, China, from 2019 to 2022. Net primary productivity (NPP) was simulated with the Carnegie–Ames–Stanford Approach (CASA) model on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform using Sentinel-2 imagery and converted to theoretical straw resources using an NPP–yield coefficient and the straw-to-grain ratio. The estimated maize straw resources were evaluated against field measurements collected in 2022, yielding an R2 of 0.63 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 849.26 kg/ha. At the county level, comparisons with statistical reference straw resources for 2019–2022 yielded R2 values of 0.84–0.86. The four-year mean straw yield was 9416 kg/ha, with precipitation as the main climatic factor shaping this pattern. In terms of utilization potential, the straw supply could meet the residue requirement of conservation tillage on 87.34% of the cultivated area, and the straw available for feed could meet approximately 70% of the straw demand of the existing cattle and sheep inventories. These results provide spatially explicit information for straw management and regional agricultural planning.

title: Deep Unfolding with Target Confidence and Cross-Stage Memory for Infrared Small Target Detection
summary: Infrared small targets occupy few pixels and often exhibit weak contrast, making them difficult to distinguish from bright edges, background clutter, and noise. Deep unfolding provides an interpretable framework for background–target decomposition, yet weak target responses may be absorbed into background estimates or suppressed during sparse updates. We propose a Target Confidence and Memory Network (TCMNet) that incorporates target confidence and cross-stage error memory into a multistage deep unfolding framework. A confidence-guided multiscale background modeling module combines smoothing priors at different scales with learned background representations. In later stages, target confidence derived from intermediate target estimates reduces the influence of potential targets on background estimation. A transform-domain sparse update module employs learnable transforms and channel-wise learnable thresholds to suppress clutter, together with local target protection to limit the attenuation of weak responses. To exploit information from preceding stages, a cross-stage error memory module integrates current target responses, inter-stage response changes, and reconstruction residuals into a recurrent state. This state produces bounded corrections to the target estimate before it is passed to the next stage. Target estimates are constrained to be nonnegative, while an auxiliary reconstruction loss penalizes discrepancies between reconstructed and observed images. A final prediction head combines target estimates, multiscale local contrast cues, and the reconstruction residual to produce a target probability map. Experiments on NUDT-SIRST and a local 1:1 partition of MDvsFA demonstrate the effectiveness of TCMNet, achieving mIoU scores of 91.71% and 90.31%, F1 scores of 95.68% and 94.91%, and detection probabilities of 98.41% and 96.84%, respectively. These results highlight the ability of the proposed framework to preserve weak target responses while suppressing background interference. By integrating explicit background–target decomposition with adaptive sparse updating and cross-stage error correction, TCMNet provides a structured approach to infrared small target detection in complex scenes.

title: Overall and Local Effects of Multi-Temporal Imagery on Rainfall-Induced Landslide Mapping
summary: Higher overall accuracy does not necessarily mean more complete landslide mapping at every location. Across eight rainfall-related events, we examine the benefits of earlier satellite imagery using U-TAE, a neural network that combines images acquired on different dates, as the main model. We compare overall accuracy with the fraction of mapped landslide area detected within local image patches. Mean average precision increased from 0.333 with a post-event image to 0.379 with a pre/post pair and 0.419 with a longer sequence. Adding earlier images to the pair improved mean average precision in seven events but slightly reduced it in Chimanimani. However, the average increase in the detected fraction across locations and regions was 1.1 percentage points (95% interval −1.3 to +3.3). This provides no clear evidence that earlier images increased the average fraction of mapped landslide area detected. The estimated gain in Italy decreased from 3.0 to 0.3 percentage points when the decision thresholds changed, indicating that the apparent improvement depended on how the predictions were converted into a landslide map. The benefit of earlier images was also greater in patches containing more mapped landslide area in some regions, but was not clearly related to the strength of surface change in patches with sufficient mapped area and usable optical observations. An auxiliary comparison with U-Net, a convolutional image-segmentation model, also showed local detection differences alongside higher overall accuracy. Local detection also varied when the same models were retrained using unchanged images. Checking local detection changes alongside conventional accuracy measures helps assess whether adding earlier imagery reduces missed landslide area across locations.

title: Benchmarking Geospatial Foundation Models Against a Supervised Baseline for Fine-Grained Alpine Habitat Change Detection with Very High-Resolution Imagery and LiDAR
summary: Geospatial foundation models (GFMs) are proposed for operational Earth observation but benchmarked mostly on urban and agricultural data, so their value and limitations for fine-grained ecological monitoring, with fuzzy class boundaries and severe class imbalance, are largely untested. We benchmark five GFMs (Clay v1.0, Clay v1.5, Prithvi-EO-2.0, DOFA, TerraMind) against two supervised U-Net baselines, one with a transformer (MiT-B2) and one with a convolutional (ResNet-50) encoder, for post-classification habitat change detection in Gesäuse National Park, Austria. All models are trained with three seeds on 2013 expert-interpreted labels (23 habitat classes), using very high-resolution red, green, blue (RGB) and near-infrared aerial imagery and a normalised digital surface model (nDSM) derived from airborne light detection and ranging (LiDAR). Applied to 2019 imagery and 2020 LiDAR, their predictions are compared with the 2013 reference to yield change maps with eight transition classes plus no change. All five GFMs are robustly ahead of the convolutional U-Net, but so is the transformer U-Net, which only Clay v1.0 exceeds, by a small margin (multi-class change macro Intersection over Union (IoU) 0.233 vs. 0.209) whose paired 95% confidence interval (+0.001 to +0.045) nearly includes zero. Adding the nDSM helps every model, but mostly in the canopy-cover classes, whose reference labels are themselves LiDAR-derived. Rare or heterogeneous transitions remain poorly detected by every model. Rule-based post-processing defined with the Gesäuse National Park administration converts the predictions into polygon-structured, ecologically plausible change maps that meet the park’s data standards, with little effect on pixel accuracy (multi-class macro IoU −0.03 to +0.04) but lower recall for forest density loss and setback; the maps are therefore suited to flagging candidate changes for expert verification rather than to unsupervised use.

title: A Combined Strategy for Detecting Cotton Seedlings in UAV RGB Images Based on GLI Automatic Annotation and Hybrid Architecture Deep Learning
summary: Accurate detection of cotton seedlings is essential for monitoring crop establishment. However, manual annotation is time-consuming, and the quality of conventional automatic annotation methods is affected by illumination and background conditions. This study proposes a joint strategy combining green leaf index (GLI) automatic annotation with deep learning detection. Three annotation methods were considered: GLI, excess green minus excess red (ExG–ExR), and hue–saturation–value (HSV). Their nine combinations with three detectors (YOLOv10n, RT-DETR-L, and Mamba-YOLO-B) were evaluated using spatial data partitioning and independent cross-region testing. Under identical post-processing, GLI achieved the highest annotation quality, with an F1 score of 96.18% and a mean intersection over union (IoU) of 89.78% for matched boxes. For initial box drawing only, bounding boxes for 200 targets were generated in 0.399 s, compared with approximately 600 s for manual drawing. Detection accuracy was assessed using mean average precision (mAP) at IoU thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95 (mAP@0.5:0.95). Across three random seeds, Mamba-YOLO + GLI achieved the highest mean source-region mAP@0.5:0.95, at 0.8020. In cross-region testing, Mamba-YOLO + GLI achieved the best detection and counting performance, with an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.3446. However, its detection accuracy remained substantially lower than in source-region testing. These results demonstrate that GLI automatic annotation can provide effective training labels for cotton seedling detection. Among the evaluated combinations, Mamba-YOLO + GLI achieved the highest mean source-region mAP@0.5:0.95 and the highest cross-region mAP@0.5:0.95.

title: Retrospective Process-Paired Assessment of Optical Availability for Sentinel-1/2 Flood Segmentation and Probability Mapping
summary: Adding optical imagery to radar can improve a flood map without improving the flood probabilities assigned to its pixels. We examine when these benefits agree, using a Sentinel-1 radar-only network as the reference for a Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 fusion network. The same flood processes and reference pixels are compared as optical input is progressively masked. With no additional masking, fusion improves mean flood-area overlap by 0.0391/0.0373 and reduces mean flood-probability squared error by 0.0203/0.0211 on 18 internal and nine held-out flood episodes previously inspected during development. When only 25% of spatial blocks are retained, overlap gains remain slightly positive, but probability error increases by 0.0106/0.0091. Most of the original-optical probability benefit comes from avoiding false flood probabilities on reference permanent water; probability improvements on reference flood pixels are inconsistent. Controls and spatial examples expose trade-offs between missed floods and false floods. Additional single-event checks reveal adverse transfer. The practical contribution is evidence that flood-area accuracy and flood-probability quality must be assessed separately when optical support changes. This retrospective satellite-image assessment relates optical availability to flood-area accuracy and probability quality.

title: DB-CASSE-Net: A Dual-Branch Network with Constrained Adaptive Spatial Sampling and Spectral Enhancement for Hyperspectral Unmixing
summary: Regular convolution is widely used in spectral–spatial unmixing networks to aggregate neighborhood information, but its fixed sampling grid cannot readily follow irregular material boundaries or elongated structures and may introduce heterogeneous pixels whose compositions differ from that of the central pixel. This study presents DB-CASSE-Net, a dual-branch hyperspectral unmixing network that combines constrained adaptive spatial sampling with spectral feature enhancement. The spatial branch learns position-dependent offsets from configurable initial sampling geometries. A hyperbolic-tangent mapping bounds the displacement range, while magnitude and spatial-smoothness regularizers suppress excessive drift and abrupt local changes. In parallel, the spectral branch uses pointwise convolutions and an identity-initialized squeeze-and-excitation mechanism to recalibrate latent spectral channels adaptively. Features from the two branches are fused, and a spectral skip connection restores fine-grained information from the original spectral signatures that may be attenuated by successive nonlinear transformations. The resulting abundance responses satisfy nonnegativity and sum-to-one constraints, and a nonnegative linear decoder reconstructs the hyperspectral image, enabling unsupervised joint estimation of endmembers and abundances. Experiments on Jasper Ridge, Samson, and Urban show that DB-CASSE-Net achieves the lowest mean abundance RMSE and mean endmember SAD among the compared methods on Jasper Ridge and Urban, and the second-lowest mean abundance RMSE on Samson.

title: Adaptive Spatial Filtering and Neural Regression Modeling for Enhanced Bathymetric Retrieval in Optically Complex Inland Waters Using PlanetScope Satellite Imagery
summary: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) in inland waters remains challenging due to the strong spatial variability of optically active constituents and limited optical penetration depth. This study investigates the impact of a proposed Adaptive Spatial Filtering (ASF) approach and nonlinear regression models on bathymetric retrieval from PlanetScope imagery in two optically complex bays of Lake Dąbie, Poland. Single-band (SBA), multi-band (MBA), and band-ratio (BR) approaches were evaluated using linear regression (LR), generalized regression neural networks (GRNN), multilayer perceptron (MLP), and radial basis function neural networks (RBFNN). The results demonstrate that the proposed ASF method improves bathymetric reconstruction accuracy and surface quality. Within the threshold depth range, the average RMSE decreased from 0.195 m to 0.156 m, while coefficients of determination reached up to R2 = 0.914. Qualitative analyses further demonstrated that ASF improved the visual and geomorphological interpretability of SDB products and the overall quality of seabed reconstruction, enabling a more faithful representation of subtle morphological features and microtopographic structures. The SBA Red configuration provided the greatest effective mapping depth, reaching 2.76 m in Lubczyna Bay, whereas the MBA approach produced the most stable performance across varying depth ranges. GRNN achieved the highest accuracy within the threshold-depth range, while all neural-network models outperformed linear regression, except for the band-ratio configuration, which showed limited suitability for bathymetric retrieval in the study areas. The results indicate that local bio-optical conditions exert a stronger influence on SDB performance than depth alone and that no single spectral configuration is universally optimal for inland-water environments. The proposed methodology demonstrates the potential of combining adaptive filtering and nonlinear regression to enhance the applicability of satellite-derived bathymetry in optically complex inland waters for hydrographic surveys and environmental monitoring.

title: UAV Thermal Screening of Landfill Gas Networks: Detection Limits, Matched Controls and Georeferencing Requirements
summary: Leaks from above-ground landfill gas pipelines are hard to locate with point-based methods. This study tested whether unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) thermography can identify potential leak zones on the gas network in a site of central Italy. Two thermal surveys (November 2023 and 2024) were processed into 8 cm thermal orthomosaics, co-registered to a median offset of 22 cm and checked on 29 RTK GNSS points. The 147 thermal anomalies identified from the ground in 2023, only one of which had measurable gas, were compared with random, distance-matched and on-pipe controls, using a local thermal metric on all pixels and on soil only. Anomaly sites were warmer than random points (AUC 0.77) but not warmer than matched or on-pipe controls once spatial dependence was considered, and showed no excess soil heat in any of 176 parameter settings. Synthetic warm spots were detected in 80% of cases above 15 °C on the pipe and 10 °C on the adjacent soil, and became undetectable with position errors of 2 m. The study thus evaluates the thermal signature of ground-identified anomalies, not leak detection rates; UAV thermography can support screening only with matched controls, accurate co-registration and gas verification.

title: Climate-Specific Nonlinear Associations Between Urban Thermal Stress and the Built Environment Across Mainland China
summary: Urban thermal stress (UTS) is intensifying, but its evolution and relationships with the built environment may differ across China’s contrasting climate zones. We examined mean summer Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) estimates for 1605 urban centres identified in the Global Human Settlement Layer Urban Centre Database (GHS-UCDB) across mainland China in 2005, 2010, 2015, and 2020. Random Forest models and interpretable machine-learning methods were used to compare national patterns with those in two humid zones. Mean UTCI increased from 29.61 °C to 30.43 °C, and 73.02% of urban centres recorded higher values in 2020 than in 2005. The increase was concentrated in humid China, reaching 1.08 °C in the tropical–subtropical humid (TSH) zone and 0.64 °C in the temperate humid and semi-humid (TH) zone. Built-environment associations also differed across the four assessment years. Nationally, the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) ranked first in 2005 and 2010, whereas surface albedo ranked first in 2015 and 2020. Regional models showed sharper contrasts. NDVI and impervious-surface proportion consistently ranked highest in TSH, whereas albedo, urban morphology, and landscape configuration were more prominent in TH. Nonlinear responses and leading interactions varied across scales, zones, and years. National models showed predominantly NDVI-related patterns in 2005 and 2010, whereas albedo-related patterns were more prominent in 2015 and 2020. NDVI–impervious cover was the leading TSH interaction in 2010, 2015, and 2020. In TH, NDVI–population density ranked first in 2005 and 2010, tree cover–built-up intensity in 2015, and albedo–tree cover in 2020. National associations therefore cannot be transferred uniformly across climate zones. These findings support climate-specific thermal-risk screening, but model-derived response ranges require local validation before application in local urban planning and design decisions.

title: Moisture and Fuel-Related Conditions Shape Regional Patterns of Predicted Forest Fire Occurrence in China
summary: Rising fire frequency and intensity under global warming challenge ecological security, yet dynamic fuel-related variables remain insufficiently represented in forest fire prediction models. This study integrated LPJ-simulated fuel variables with five machine learning algorithms to assess their contribution to fire prediction across China. SHAP and partial dependence analyses examined predictor importance and responses in northeastern (NEF), southeastern (SEF), and southwestern (SWF) forests. Future fire occurrence (2041–2100) was projected with bias-corrected CMIP6 data under three SSP scenarios. The main findings were as follows: (1) Fuel inclusion improved model performance by approximately 2–4% under spatial cross-validation, with CatBoost showing favorable overall performance. (2) Predictor importance differed across regions and forest types. Aboveground litter carbon storage (LitterC) and vapor pressure deficit (VPD) were the leading predictors in northeastern coniferous forests; elevation (DEM) and soil moisture (SM) were important in the SWF; and SM ranked first in both SEF types. Partial dependence analyses revealed nonlinear responses, with prominent fuel-related patterns in the NEF and soil moisture-related patterns in the SWF and SEF. (3) Future predictions increased overall in the SWF and SEF, with larger absolute increases in the SEF. Increased predictions covered 66–69% of SWF forests and 74.80–94.01% of SEF forests. Although the NEF showed an overall decline in regional mean predictions, localized increases remained evident. These findings support integrating dynamic fuel information into fire prediction and identifying priority areas for future monitoring and management.

title: SGFAR-YOLO: Semantic-Guided Multiscale Fusion and Anisotropic Refinement for Satellite Instance Segmentation and UAV-Based Damage Localization of Waterway Regulation Structures
summary: Regional inventories and local condition assessment of waterway regulation structures require complementary observations from satellite and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery. Automated interpretation must preserve elongated structures with weak boundaries while separating targets from complex river backgrounds. We propose semantic-guided multiscale fusion and anisotropic refinement YOLO (SGFAR-YOLO), a novel pre-head feature design for independently trained satellite instance segmentation and UAV-oriented detection models. A semantic-guided feature pyramid network (SGFPN) coordinates coarse semantics and fine detail, while the residual strip enhancement module (RSEM) provides gated local and axial context at high-resolution pyramid levels. On the satellite validation split, SGFAR-YOLO achieves 57.31% horizontal-bounding-box AP and 43.14% mask AP, exceeding the YOLO11 baseline by 3.11 and 2.80 percentage points. UAV-oriented box AP reaches 34.75%, a gain of 5.71 percentage points. Ablation studies and qualitative comparisons examine the design across both tasks and illustrate boundary continuity, small-target recovery, and localization of surface damage conditions. The proposed method provides a practical framework for regional mapping of waterway regulation structures and local screening of their surface condition within the Jingjiang reach.

title: An Accurate Slant Range Inversion Algorithm and Its Application in FDS-PolSAR Polarimetric Calibration
summary: Frequency-division multi-polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (FDS-PolSAR) achieves simultaneous multi-polarimetric observation through a carrier frequency offset, which fundamentally eliminates temporal decorrelation in dynamic scenarios, but the four polarimetric channels do not share a common frequency basis, and the global scalar phase assumption of the classical Whitt general calibration technique (GCT) is structurally invalid, causing complete calibration failure for point-like targets. Conventional SAR ranging and differential Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)/strapdown inertial navigation systems (INSs) only provide centimeter-level accuracy, which cannot satisfy the precision requirements for inter-frequency phase compensation. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an accurate slant range inversion (ASRI)-assisted polarimetric calibration scheme. The ASRI algorithm extracts the pure quadratic phase component of target echoes via a Deskew–Filtering–Recovery (DFR) chain and provides millimeter-level equivalent accuracy for polarimetric calibration by correlation matching with a digital twin phase library. The inter-frequency phase difference is pre-compensated using the inverted slant range, which restores the validity of the GCT framework. Calibration experiments validate that the proposed method improves the cross-polarization isolation to 40.31 dB and reduces co-polarization phase imbalance to 3.1°, and this residual phase imbalance corresponds to a slant range error equivalent of approximately 2.2 mm as a conservative indirect indicator of inversion performance.

title: Plot-Level Yield Modelling of Winter Triticale from Multi-Temporal UAV Multispectral Indices: Validation Across Plots and Seasons
summary: Reported accuracy of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based yield models depends on whether validation respects repeated plots and seasonal variation. We tested whether temporal descriptors of vegetation indices explain plot-level grain yield of winter triticale and whether it transfers between years. Here, 7 multispectral UAV flights within 190–245 days after sowing were analysed for 20 fixed plots in 2024 and 2025. For normalised difference vegetation index (NDVI), green normalised difference vegetation index (GNDVI), normalised difference red-edge (NDRE), optimised soil-adjusted vegetation index (OSAVI), and wide dynamic range vegetation index (WDRVI), the temporal mean, median, standard deviation, and normalised area under the curve gave 20 candidate predictors. Single-index and multi-index models, with predictors selected by Elastic Net stability selection or a genetic algorithm, were evaluated by nested plot-grouped cross-validation and leave-one-year-out (LOYO) validation against season-mean references. Pooled R2 reached 0.89 (RMSE = 433 kg ha−1; WDRVI–KNN), but a season-mean reference alone gave 0.83. Within 2024, the best models reduced root mean square error (RMSE) from 571 to about 290–380 kg ha−1; within 2025, none improved on the reference. In leave-one-year-out validation, the lowest RMSE (about 2.0 t ha−1) was only 20% below that of the training-season mean (2.5 t ha−1), and all R2 values were negative. Yield differences between control and manured plots reversed direction between seasons (−328 and +300 kg ha−1, both 95% confidence intervals included zero) and are confounded with plot position. The descriptors can rank plot conditions within a season, but two seasons do not support yield forecasting for unseen years.

title: Reconstruction of Paleo-Channels Around the Tang Wang Cheng Site in Xinjiang, China, Discerned from Multi-Source Remote Sensing and OSL Dating
summary: The development of drainage systems is essential for sustaining oasis vitality and human habitation in arid and semi-arid regions. The Tang Wang Cheng Site (TWCS) is located in the desert-oasis ecotone at the northwestern edge of the Taklamakan Desert. Archaeological evidence from reclamation zones and irrigation channels at the site indicates a substantial historical reliance on water resources, in sharp contrast to the current arid conditions. However, the processes of paleo-drainage reorganization and associated environmental evolution around the TWCS remain poorly understood. In this study, paleo-channel traces were mapped through geomorphological interpretation of multi-source remote sensing data, supported by field investigations, geomorphological surveys, and archaeological excavations. Sedimentary stratigraphic analysis and optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating were used to investigate local changes in depositional conditions. The results reveal numerous paleo-channel traces west of and within the TWCS, indicating a high concentration of former channel features around the site. Five OSL ages from a natural profile approximately 11 km northwest of the TWCS constrain local depositional changes between approximately 1500 and 710 yr B.P., including a transition from gravel-dominated to sand-dominated sedimentation. Excavated channel deposits within the site provide evidence of fluvial activity during its occupation. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating historical satellite imagery and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-derived terrain data for mapping paleo-channel traces in arid archaeological landscapes and provide a basis for further investigation of hydrological change and settlement dynamics in southern Xinjiang.

title: A Multilayer Drought Framework Reveals Groundwater-Linked Vegetation Loss in Water-Limited Northern China
summary: Vegetation restoration can increase vegetation cover while raising water demand in water-limited regions. Most drought-vegetation assessments focus on atmospheric and soil moisture droughts. The added value of groundwater information remains insufficiently quantified. This study developed a multilayer drought-vegetation loss framework for northern China during 2003–2022. It linked three single and four Copula-based compound drought types to leaf area index (LAI) negative-anomaly events. Compared with the atmosphere-soil framework, adding groundwater enabled additional drought matches for 16.3% of all assessable LAI loss events, including those unmatched by either framework. Most additions involved groundwater co-occurring with or connecting other water-stress layers. Compound drought dominated areas expanded from 20.7% to 58.6% of the valid area between 2003–2012 and 2013–2022. Groundwater-drought-dominated areas increased from 4.3% to 21.2%. Groundwater drought showed the most pronounced nonlinear association with cumulative relative vegetation loss (LOSStot) among single drought types. LOSStot peaked near an index of −2.16 and declined at more negative values. XGBoost-SHAP analysis identified event-period hydroclimatic anomalies as the largest contributor to relative predictive importance. These findings support ecological restoration planning tailored to local drought characteristics, water availability and vegetation vulnerability.

title: WastePNOA: A Dataset for Waste Disposal Site Detection Using PNOA Imagery
summary: Improper disposal of solid waste is a major source of environmental pollution, making timely detection essential for protecting environmental and human health. Although several remote sensing datasets have recently been proposed for solid waste detection, most are limited in terms of spatial coverage, temporal diversity, annotation quality, and resolution. In this work, we introduce WastePNOA, a publicly available dataset based on Very-High-Resolution (VHR) aircraft imagery from the Spanish National Aerial Orthophotography Plan, also known as PNOA. The dataset comprises 24,884 images from 132 landfill areas across Spain between 2013 and 2023. The dataset provides pixel-level annotations across three semantic classes: waste, leachate pond, and background. We introduce two dataset distributions, WastePNOA-Spatial and WastePNOA-Temporal, to investigate the presence of waste across geographically unseen areas and the temporal evolution of previously observed areas, respectively, while also assessing the effect of background-only images. SegFormer consistently achieves the strongest overall performance, reaching 58.59% and 67.30% foreground-only mIoU for spatial and temporal generalization, respectively. Results also highlight the importance of background-only images for robust performance under realistic background-dominant scenes, while indicating that retaining all such images may be redundant. Overall, WastePNOA provides a challenging benchmark for solid waste disposal site detection and supports future research in remote-sensing-based environmental monitoring.

title: Time-Series InSAR-Constrained Spatiotemporal Evolution and Driving Factors of a Loess Landslide: A Case Study of the Li-Kan Highway Landslide on the Loess Plateau
summary: Loess landslides exhibit strong spatial heterogeneity and complex rainfall responses, making their evolution difficult to characterize from one-dimensional deformation observations alone. This study investigates the Li-Kan Highway landslide on the right bank of the Lijiaxia Reservoir, China, by integrating ascending- and descending-track time-series InSAR, aspect-parallel flow (APF) constrained three-dimensional deformation reconstruction, the Comprehensive Standardized Deformation Index (CSDI), wavelet-based rainfall-response analysis, and Massflow numerical simulation. The reconstructed deformation field shows that the landslide is dominated by northeastward horizontal motion, while local sectors exhibit distinct movement directions and deformation components, indicating multiple kinematic units. Along the approximately 2 km P–P′ profile, the north–south, east–west, and vertical deformation–velocity components exhibit spatially variable patterns, consistent with heterogeneous slope kinematics. Principal component analysis shows that the first two components explain 85.6% of the total variance, summarizing the spatial variability. CSDI analysis of representative points P1–P3 reveals asynchronous deformation activity: P1 is mainly active in autumn 2018, P2 shows enhanced activity in 2019 and spring–summer 2020, and P3 exhibits a weaker local increase around mid-2021. In particular, the 2020 response at P2 is interpreted as a local kinematic adjustment rather than synchronous acceleration of the entire slope. Because no overall failure occurred during the observation period, CSDI-defined Stage III is treated as enhanced deformation activity rather than a direct failure criterion. Continuous wavelet transform and time-lag cross-correlation indicate significant rainfall-related temporal responses, with deformation lagging rainfall by approximately 12, 108, and 36 days at P1, P2, and P3, respectively. Massflow simulation of a potential frontal failure scenario shows a rapid transition from source-area release to channelized high-speed runout and frontal deposition. The maximum simulated velocity reaches approximately 22.6 m/s in the main transport channel, while the frontal deposit exceeds 16 m in thickness and remains about 13.6 m at 200 s. The total simulated mass decreases by only about 0.38%, indicating good numerical mass conservation. These results demonstrate that the Li-Kan Highway landslide evolves through spatially heterogeneous and temporally asynchronous deformation, with rainfall responses varying among slope sectors. The integrated framework links long-term deformation monitoring, stage identification, rainfall-response analysis, and potential failure simulation, providing a practical basis for interpreting the evolution and hazard potential of large loess landslides.

title: SSWR-YOLO: Lightweight Vessel Detection for Shipborne HFSWR in Complex Maritime Scenarios
summary: Shipborne high-frequency surface wave radar (SHFSWR) plays a critical role in maritime surveillance but suffers from severe performance degradation in complex maritime scenarios characterized by sea clutter, dense target aggregation, and weak echo returns. To address these challenges, we propose Shipborne Surface Wave Radar You Only Look Once (SSWR-YOLO), a lightweight detection network built upon the YOLOv8 framework with specialized modules for robust detection under adverse conditions. Specifically, a receptive field spatial attention convolution is embedded into the backbone to dynamically enhance target responses relative to broadened sea clutter and highlight weak target features. Furthermore, a context aggregation network is integrated into the neck to enhance multi-scale feature fusion, effectively resolving target masking in dense vessel target scenarios. Additionally, a softened non-maximum suppression strategy is employed to prevent the erroneous removal of overlapped vessel proposals. Experimental results on both simulated and field SHFSWR data demonstrate that, on the 50 held-out test images, SSWR-YOLO achieves a 9.76 percentage point improvement in detection rate and a 3.11% reduction in overall false discovery rate over the baseline YOLOv8, while introducing only marginal parameter overhead. The proposed method offers an efficient and reliable solution for vessel detection under challenging maritime conditions, with a core network forward pass compatible with near-real-time processing on a desktop GPU and potential for embedded deployment.

title: MSTrack: Multi-Modal Feature Aggregation and Spatio-Temporal Memory Context Encoding for Ground and UAV RGB-Thermal Infrared Tracking
summary: RGB-thermal infrared (RGBT) target tracking integrates spatial features of both RGB and thermal infrared (TIR) modalities, providing a discriminative basis for target feature representation and state estimation. However, existing methods suffer from insufficient cross-modal feature interaction and inadequate spatio-temporal contextual correlation, which limits tracking stability and accuracy in challenging scenarios. To address these issues, we propose MSTrack, a novel tracker that integrates a multi-modal feature aggregation (MMFA) module and a spatio-temporal memory context encoding (STMCE) module. First, to capture both shared features and complementary details across modalities, we design the MMFA module, which employs parallel Swin Transformers and four cross-modal feature interaction (CMFI) components to achieve progressive fusion of RGB and TIR features. Specifically, CMFI integrates a cross-modal collaborative attention mechanism, a triplet attention mechanism, a bidirectional cross-modal weighted fusion mechanism, and a multi-stage information aggregation mechanism to achieve cross-modal interactions. Second, to fuse the key spatio-temporal features across multiple frames, we design the STMCE module. This STMCE module leverages a historical feature memory pool (HFMP) and a spatio-temporal context encoder (STCE) to model global dependencies among the template, current, and historical frames. Finally, the prediction head outputs the target bounding box. Experiments on four ground-based RGBT datasets demonstrate that the proposed tracker outperforms other state-of-the-art trackers. Furthermore, the results on the UAV-based VTUAV dataset validate its generalization potential. Specifically, MSTrack achieves PR/SR scores of 0.877/0.637 on RGBT234 and 0.669/0.530 on LasHeR. On the VTUAV dataset, it achieves MPR/MSR scores of 0.812/0.672 on the short-term subset and 0.595/0.501 on the long-term subset.

title: A High-Precision Three-Dimensional Branch Reconstruction Method for Tree Morphological Phenotype
summary: The three-dimensional architecture of the trunk and branch system of individual trees constitutes essential information for tree breeding trait evaluation, the construction of functional-structural plant models (FSPM), and precision forest management; its morphological traits are typically represented by diameter at breast height (DBH), tree height, branch order, and the 3D branching topology. In recent years, point-cloud-based tree structure parsing has advanced rapidly. However, constrained by field acquisition conditions and sensor principles, tree point clouds commonly exhibit missing data and noise, causing locally non-uniform density and introducing noise interference. Under these conditions, traditional QSM (Quantitative Structure Models) tend to produce cross-section distortion and inflated volume, degrading both modeling accuracy and the reliability of parameter extraction; moreover, their radius estimation usually relies on species-specific calibration, limiting cross-species application. To address these limitations, this study proposes a high-precision three-dimensional reconstruction method for the trunk and branch system to extract tree morphological phenotypes, which achieves robust reconstruction under noise and missing data through density-adaptive clustering and biologically mechanistic self-adaptive WBE radius simulation. Experimental results show that, compared with existing mainstream methods, the proposed method yields better modeling performance and stronger robustness on both artificial and real branch point clouds, reaching centimeter-level accuracy.

title: A Semantic–Geometric Collaborative Framework for Roof Plane Segmentation in Airborne LiDAR Point Clouds
summary: Roof plane segmentation from airborne light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point clouds provides planar patches for reconstructing 3D roof surfaces and their structural relationships. Existing methods still find it difficult to balance semantic awareness and geometric consistency, especially in the presence of ambiguous boundaries between adjacent roof planes, scattered outlier or non-roof points, and diverse roof structures. To address this problem, this paper proposes a semantic–geometric collaborative framework for roof plane segmentation that uses semantic segmentation results to guide geometric clustering. First, semantic segmentation identifies planar interiors and inter-plane boundaries, with an additional noise or non-roof class where applicable. Second, a k-nearest neighbor (KNN) local-priority clustering method is designed to generate the initial segmentation. It selects seeds from reliable planar interiors and uses a double-ended queue to guide roof plane clusters to grow from stable interior regions toward uncertain boundaries. Third, a multi-neighbor edge growth (MEG) strategy with adaptive residual constraints is introduced to refine the initial segmentation. For each initial roof plane, the plane model and residual threshold are estimated from its own geometric distribution, and the remaining unassigned non-noise points are assigned according to point-to-plane distances and neighboring plane relationships. Under the evaluation procedure used in this study, the proposed method achieves strong instance-level scores and competitive point-level scores on the WHU-Roof, RoofN3D, and Building3D datasets. On the WHU-Roof dataset, it achieves 86.8% coverage (Cov), 91.3% weighted coverage (WCov), and 97.4% F1-score. On the RoofN3D dataset, it achieves the highest Cov of 85.6%, with a WCov of 90.3%. On the Building3D dataset, it achieves 82.7% Cov, 88.4% WCov, and 95.8% F1-score. These results support combining semantic boundary information with geometric clustering to separate adjacent roof planes and refine their boundaries on the evaluated datasets.

title: Regional-scale field-level estimation and mapping of tillage practices in areas with crop diversity
summary: The imperative for sustainable agriculture has led to the promotion of conservation tillage practices, which are critical for maintaining soil health and reducing negative environmental impacts. However, the ability to verify the adoption of these practices at a regional scale and with minimal costs remains a challenge, particularly in regions with diverse crop systems. This study presents a satellite-imagery-based random forest classifier that integrates crop class information and a customized importance weighting technique for field-level, regional-scale mapping of tillage practices in crop-diverse regions. We use eastern Washington State, U.S., with multiple grains, legumes, and canola as a case study. Using 577 field-level ground-truth data points across two counties, the tillage classifier achieved a median overall accuracy of 84%, representing a 15 percentage point improvement over the baseline median overall accuracy of 69%, driven by the inclusion of crop class and the application of importance weighting. Specific crop classes, including grains, legumes, and canola, showed accuracy improvements of 6, 42, and 13 percentage points, respectively. While the model showed promising results, limitations such as overprediction of no-tillage in non-grain crop classes were identified, pointing to the need for further refinement with additional data. The model was applied to map tillage practices across dryland fields in eastern Washington State for the years 2012, 2017, and 2022, and the predictions were generally congruent with the USDA Census of Agriculture county-level statistics. This research offers a scalable tool for the verification of conservation tillage practice adoption, supporting both regional and global monitoring efforts for sustainable agricultural practices.

title: Temperature and emissivity retrieval from airborne hyperspectral thermal infrared imagery using adaptive continuous piecewise linear modeling with water vapor scaling

title: Monte Carlo biphasic estimation of fire properties (McBEF): Part I, algorithm formulation
summary: Sub-pixel fire characterization is essential for quantifying wildfire energetics, combustion phase dynamics, and their atmospheric impacts from satellite observations. This study presents a series of Observing System Simulation Experiments (OSSEs) to systematically evaluate the influence of temperature phase complexity, channel selection, and intra-phase temperature heterogeneity on the performance of a Bayesian retrieval framework. Using synthetic observations derived from a multi-phase radiance model, we assess retrieval skill across key fire properties—including Fire Radiative Power (FRP), visible energy fraction (VEF), and flaming heat flux—under realistic sensor constraints. Results show that a bi-phasic fire model provides a strong balance between accuracy and observational feasibility, outperforming conventional approaches such as Wooster’s FRP regression, particularly in low-intensity fire scenarios. FRP is the retrieved quantity most resilient to model and observational uncertainties, while VEF and heat flux estimates are more sensitive to both fire phase partitioning and spectral coverage. Shortwave and mid-infrared bands, especially the day–night band (DNB) and 2.25 μ m channels, are shown to offer the greatest constraint on retrieval accuracy. We further analyze the impact of intra-phase temperature variability and propose practical filtering strategies for identifying low-confidence cases, such as smoldering-dominated fires. The theoretical framework is applicable to multi-channel fire observations more generally, while its companion Part II implementation focuses specifically on nighttime VIIRS observations.

title: Toward a global snow water equivalent observing strategy
summary: Current snow observations do not meet the data requirements established by the 2017 Decadal Survey and the Global Climate Observing System (GCOS) for global snow water equivalent (SWE) measurements. This paper evaluates existing spaceborne assets for global SWE and snow depth monitoring and identifies critical observational gaps that necessitate a dedicated snow observing strategy. We review snow data requirements across multiple application areas, including water resources, climate monitoring, weather forecasting, and disaster management, demonstrating the need for SWE measurements at 100 m to 4 km spatial resolution with 1- to 5-day temporal frequency and 10–20% accuracy. Analysis of current capabilities from missions including AMSR2, Sentinel-1, NISAR, and ICESat-2 reveals that while these sensors provide valuable SWE and depth information, they cannot, even when combined, deliver the comprehensive, high-resolution SWE data required for operational and scientific applications, observing only 40–60% of the global snowpack on a daily to weekly basis. We propose a global snow observing strategy centered on a core radar-based snow mission that would serve as the reference standard for a constellation of complementary sensors. This approach, combined with existing observations, ancillary data, advanced data fusion techniques, and land surface models, would provide accurate and timely SWE data essential for water resource management, climate research, and hazard mitigation.
