title: Hierarchical active learning for annotation-efficient 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing
summary: 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing remains challenging because sparse returns, irregular layouts, heavy occlusion, and diverse machinery make object representation and localization difficult. Dense manual annotation in such scenes is also inefficient and costly, creating a strong need for annotation-efficient learning. Existing active-learning methods often struggle in this setting because they tend to favor uncertain but redundant samples while overlooking representative scene coverage. To address this problem, we propose Hierarchical Clustering-enhanced Active Learning (HCAL), an active-learning framework for LiDAR-based 3D object detection in construction and roadwork environments. HCAL improves sample selection under limited labeling budgets by identifying informative candidate keyframes, suppressing redundant uncertain samples, and preserving representative coverage through entropy filtering, gradient-space clustering, and density-consistency selection. To support field-relevant evaluation, we further establish ConVeh3D as a construction-scene LiDAR benchmark for annotation-efficient 3D detection and unknown-category-aware evaluation in a controlled category-withheld setting. Experiments on ConVeh3D, with KITTI as secondary supporting evidence, show that HCAL achieves the best average detection accuracy across most tested labeling budgets. The results indicate that HCAL provides an effective framework for improving sample efficiency in construction-scene LiDAR-based 3D object detection under limited labeling budgets. The dataset and code will be made available at https://github.com/zxk688/ConVeh3D .

title: PSGRNet: Multi-scale spectral–frequency representation learning with gated residual fusion for coastal wetland classification using UAV hyperspectral imagery
summary: Coastal wetlands are characterized by diverse vegetation, high spectral similarity, fragmented spatial distributions, and dynamic environmental conditions, posing significant challenges for accurate hyperspectral image classification. Although UAV hyperspectral imagery provides fine-grained spatial and spectral observations that can help capture such complex and fragmented features, effectively leveraging this information to distinguish spectrally similar and spatially intermixed vegetation types remains an open problem. Therefore, we propose a Progressive Spectral Gated Residual Network (PSGRNet). Specifically, a spectral enhancement and multi-scale sequence modeling strategy is first introduced to strengthen discriminative spectral representations and capture multi-scale spectral dependencies. Building on these enhanced representations, a frequency-aware module further exploits global frequency-domain characteristics to aggregate informative spectral features adaptively. To effectively integrate both spectral and frequency-domain representations, a GRF strategy is developed to improve the robustness of the network in heterogeneous and fragmented coastal wetland scenes. We have collected three UAV-based hyperspectral datasets covering representative coastal wetland scenarios, including reed-dominated natural wetlands (NT-YK), highly fragmented landscapes with dynamic land-cover transitions (YC-YS), and human-influenced estuarine environments (LYG-LH). Experimental results on these three datasets demonstrate that PSGRNet outperforms 9 representative methods, achieving macro F1 scores of 89.25%, 81.99%, and 81.29%, respectively. These results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method for accurate coastal wetland classification and demonstrate the value of the released datasets. The datasets will be publicly available at https://github.com/HAPPYFST/Wetland-HSI-Data .

title: How should rural residential land in metropolitan suburbs be governed in the future? Evidence from Beijing using RGB-encoded multidimensional drivers and CNN prediction
summary: Rural residential land in metropolitan suburbs often expands, stabilizes and contracts within the same region, making static zoning inadequate for anticipatory governance. Existing land-use prediction approaches commonly use attribute vectors or remotely sensed image features, limiting their ability to reduce input dimensionality while preserving the spatial structure and combined effects of locational, accessibility and planning-related drivers. This study converts abstract geospatial drivers into red–green–blue (RGB) images and integrates them with convolutional neural network (CNN) models and ensemble prediction. Using suburban Beijing as a case, we evaluated 78 three-driver configurations across five deep-learning architectures, yielding 390 models. The modified VGG16 model achieved a weighted F1 score of 0.749. The optimal configuration combined village size, distance to the city center and expressway accessibility, indicating that rural residential land change is mainly associated with local development inertia, metropolitan gradients and external connectivity. A model using all nine drivers as nine-band input achieved a weighted F1 score of 0.758, compared with 0.749 for the three-driver RGB model; the latter used substantially fewer drivers while retaining higher precision and clearer variable semantics. Under the 2035 planning scenario, 36.57% of valid grids were predicted to increase, 33.90% to remain unchanged, 0.26% to decrease, and 29.27% were identified as uncertainty areas. These areas require flexible planning, dynamic monitoring and the avoidance of premature rigid decisions. By linking Earth Observation-derived land-change data with spatially structured driver representations, the workflow supports the explanation and prediction of land-use transitions and more adaptive governance of metropolitan suburbs.

title: A spatially and temporally comparable Remote Sensing Ecological Index via de-gradient national PCA for China’s resource-based cities
summary: Tracking the ecological quality of many cities over many years needs a Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) that stays comparable across space and time, yet standard constructions do not deliver one. A single national principal component analysis (PCA) is dominated by the between-city climate gradient, which loads heat and wetness with the wrong sign and inverts the index. We build a de-gradient national PCA (de-gradient PCA) whose weights come from the within-city component covariance under a fixed global normalization. The resulting index recovers the expected component signs where the single national PCA inverts them. It agrees with MODIS net primary productivity, an external ecological reference (city-mean r = 0.59 ), even after controlling for greenness (partial r = 0.50 ), and its weights are stable to city resampling and to leaving out any representative year. Applied to all 125 prefecture-level resource-based cities of China over 2003–2023, mean RSEI rose from 0.61 to 0.65 ( p < 1 0 − 4 ), with 83% of cities on a rising trend, faster than in 245 non-resource cities. Resource type set the ecological level more than development stage, and 13 cities in the arid northwest and coal belt stayed near 0.30. A spatial Durbin model identifies built-up land as the strongest local pressure and industrial structure as a persistent negative regional spillover; random-forest importance corroborates the built-up ranking.

title: Satellite embedding‑based mapping of grassland mowing frequency and its response to drought in Denmark
summary: Mowing frequency is a primary indicator of grassland management intensity, forage productivity, and biogeochemical dynamics. Yet, despite a growing body of literature, operational frameworks capable of mapping cutting regimes at a regional scale remain computationally demanding and lack independent benchmarking. Here, we evaluate the potential of Google AlphaEarth annual satellite embeddings to map grassland mowing frequency across Denmark (2017–2023) at 10-m resolution. Using farmer logs across multiple years (n = 346), Random Forest emerged as the top-performing classifier, achieving an overall accuracy of 0.73 and a macro F1-score of 0.65. Our workflow substantially outperformed the operational Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) Grassland Mowing Events (GRAME) benchmark (overall accuracy of 0.24). Latent embedding dimensions strongly correlated with macro-climatic and vegetation drivers (|ρ| > 0.8). Once deployed across the full nation extent, under 6 min of computing time, the model predictions proved ecologically consistent across pedological and agronomic gradients. We further applied Dirichlet regression to quantify how hydrological drought, indexed by a 6-month scale Standardised Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI-6), affects national mowing patterns. The extreme 2018 drought triggered a landscape-wide management de-intensification, shifting the intensive (≥4 cuts) regime into a 2 cuts system. During moderate droughts, regional responses diverged sharply: western regions exhibited agronomic resilience, whereas drier eastern islands repeatedly reverted to lower-intensity management. These results demonstrate that satellite foundation models can underpin scalable, automated agronomic monitoring and reveal grassland management’s acute sensitivity to drought, insights essential for adaptive land-use planning and national-scale environmental reporting.

title: Multi-angular remote sensing-derived directional fractional vegetation cover for improved C-factor estimation in RUSLE modeling
summary: The cover and management factor ( C -factor) is a crucial parameter influencing the accuracy of soil erosion model estimates. However, conventional approaches often overlook the influence of vegetation vertical structure, particularly understory vegetation, which may lead to biased estimation of erosion severity. To address this issue, a synergistic C -factor estimation framework was developed that integrates multi-angular remote sensing (RS) observations and directional fractional vegetation cover ( DFVC ) to enhance the characterization of vegetation structure and improve C -factor estimation accuracy. The PROSAIL model was used to simulate canopy reflectance under different viewing angles, from which a dataset of multi-angular vegetation indices (VIs) was constructed. Among these VIs, the index most strongly correlated with leaf area index ( LAI ) was selected to develop a progressive “VIs– LAI – DFVC – C -factor” estimation model. The applicability of the method was further evaluated using field measurements collected across different vegetation types and structural conditions. The perpendicular vegetation index ( PVI ) was found to be significantly correlated with LAI and was identified as the optimal feature for LAI retrieval. Among the multi-angular combinations, the three-angle combination of 0°, 36°, and 55° was retained for LAI retrieval and achieved an RMSE of 0.233 and a MAPE of 0.059. Based on the overall evaluation, the 0° + 36° configuration was adopted for final DFVC -based C -factor mapping. The proposed estimation framework demonstrated high reliability ( R 2 = 0.754), with a mean C -factor estimate value of 0.019 in the study area. This study highlights the importance of incorporating vegetation vertical structure information in C -factor estimation and demonstrates that multi-angular RS can offer effective complementary information for characterizing structural features such as canopy gaps and directional occlusion. The proposed framework presents a new approach for quantitative soil erosion monitoring and environmental management.

title: SGDiff-OS: a semantic-guided diffusion model for SAR oil spill scattering and mask field generation
summary: Marine oil spill remote sensing relies heavily on high-quality annotated data, yet the limited availability of well-annotated SAR oil spill samples with backscatter information and structural labels remains a challenge. To address the lack of structural consistency and scattering representation of existing generation methods, this study proposes a Semantic-Guided Diffusion for SAR Oil Spill Generation model (SGDiff-OS) for the joint generation of SAR oil spill backscatter coefficient σ° and corresponding binary oil spill labels, trained on a self-constructed SAR oil spill dataset. The model adopts a dual-channel conditional diffusion framework and incorporates semantic modulation to encode prior knowledge of spotted, blocky and slender morphologies, thereby improving structural representation and category controllability. Experimental results demonstrate that the generated samples show general agreement with real data in visual quality and overall statistical trends, although measurable distributional differences remain. The global mean σ° differs by approximately 1.96 dB between the real and generated samples. The generated samples retain the lower-backscatter relationship of oil-covered regions relative to seawater, although the oil-water contrast decreases from 6.59 dB to 4.65 dB. Furthermore, in an expert annotation evaluation of generated image mask pairs, the generated masks achieve an mIoU of 0.7658 and an F1-score of 0.8637 when evaluated against reference annotations. Under limited training data conditions, incorporating generated samples leads to a maximum improvement of 24.2% in mIoU, suggesting its potential value for sample augmentation under limited training conditions. These results demonstrate that the proposed model can generate SAR oil spill samples with the dominant scattering trends of real SAR data, providing supplementary data for oil spill detection and segmentation tasks.

title: A rapid and robust scheme for CFOSAT SWIM nadir SWH retrieval
summary: The Surface Waves Investigation and Monitoring (SWIM) onboard the China-France Oceanography Satellite (CFOSAT) has acquired unprecedented global ocean wave direction spectrum information. Additionally, it incorporates a nadir observation mode for significant wave height (SWH) based on principles analogous to conventional altimeters, which serves to calibrate the total energy of the wave spectrum. The retrieval of SWH from such nadir radar observations generally employs theoretical models to retrack the waveforms reflected by the sea surface, a method that demonstrates high accuracy in the open ocean environment. However, obtaining SWH using traditional retracking algorithms is computationally expensive. Furthermore, in coastal regions, waveforms are affected by factors such as the presence of land and sea ice, which means that the SWH retrieval relying on theoretical models often either fails or yields substantial errors. Leveraging the fact that SWIM does not necessitate precise ranging, we bypassed the decades-old retracking paradigm by developing dual neural network inversion models. These models perform direct SWH estimation following an initial classification of SWIM nadir waveforms. The first model targets standard open-sea waveforms, while the second is designed for coastal and sea-ice 'ocean-like' waveforms that deviate from normal patterns yet retain essential wave information. The results show that the normal-ocean model achieves a processing speed over 13 times faster than the MLE4 algorithm and nearly 22 times faster than the adaptive retracking algorithm, while maintaining comparable accuracy (RMSE = 0.31 m) to the SWIM nadir SWH product. Meanwhile, the ocean-like model enhances both the quantity and quality of usable SWH data in non-open ocean areas, leveraging the accurate mapping relationships established by the neural networks. Generally, a rapid and robust scheme was developed in this paper for retrieving nadir SWH from CFOSAT SWIM, providing an alternative methodology for retrieving nadir geophysical parameters in future nadir-looking radar systems.

title: Mapping small water bodies and their dynamics with deep learning: fusion of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery at semi-monthly 10 m spatial resolution
summary: Mapping small water body (SWB) dynamics at high spatiotemporal resolution remains challenging because optical imagery is frequently obscured by clouds, whereas SAR imagery is affected by speckle noise and blurred boundaries. Existing Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion methods often have limited capability in fully exploiting the complementary information of the two sensors, leading to uncertainties in SWB mapping. Here we propose a deep learning-based method, the multiscale global-local water feature fusion network (MGLWNet), to map semi-monthly SWB dynamics via deep fusion of time-series Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery. A large-scale dataset containing 1,193,347 SWBs (<10 ha) was constructed. MGLWNet incorporates a cloud detection branch to improve feature discrimination under cloud-contaminated conditions and a multiscale global-local feature module that combines atrous spatial pyramid pooling and multi-scale self-attention to capture both fine spatial details and global contextual information. When tested on cloud-free and cloud-contaminated datasets, MGLWNet outperformed Random Forest and several state-of-the-art deep learning models. Compared with Sentinel-1-based surface water mapping, the proposed fusion strategy substantially reduced commission errors, while the cloud detection branch effectively decreased omission errors in cloudy regions. MGLWNet was applied to map semi-monthly 10 m surface water dynamics in high-density SWB areas of Hubei Province (185,900 km2) over the period 2017–2024. Unbiased accuracy estimates were performed for validation. The semi-monthly surface water maps have a producer's accuracy of 87.65% (±2.50%) and user's accuracy of 93.11% (±2.62%), respectively, with a 95% confidence interval. Compared with Landsat-based products, the method captured more frequent intra-monthly SWB variations and detected more long-term changes (e.g. the appearance and disappearance of small ponds). The resulting high-temporal-resolution dataset further enabled characterization of multiple SWB change types, including stable seasonal water, water gain, water loss, dry periods, and wet periods. This study highlights the importance of deep learning and image fusion for characterizing spatiotemporal continuous SWB dynamics.
